title: MOO-104 disposed — the drafted G 4 clause withdrawn as fatal, 169 characters enacted instead, and applied as store revision 37 of bill-text-s8
body:
# MOO-97 record — MOO-104's counsel review disposed: the drafted G 4 clause withdrawn as fatal, two minimal cures drafted, and the death case put to the Policy Director

**MOO-97 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

**This is an internal working draft. It is not a Division of Legislative Services bill, no part of it has
been reviewed by counsel or by DLS, and no part of it is legally sufficient for introduction.** Only DLS
drafts official bills.

> **Status in one paragraph.** [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) returned **15 findings — 1 fatal, 5
> serious, 6 moderate, 3 minor** — on the 68-word subdivision G 4 clause drafted but never applied
> and on two notice sentences that were never in the bill. **The clause is withdrawn. None of its 68
> words survives.** In its place, **169 characters in one anchor**, both changes inside subdivision G 4.
> **APPLIED.** The two cures are in the live text as **store revision 37** of
> [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) (document revision **41**, base
> `22f099d4-23f7-4f41-9f9f-d485226225b9`, final **521,007** characters against the 524,288-character
> ceiling, headroom **3,281**). The labels moved under the plan and are stated as applied: the §7 items
> are **59, 60 and 61**, the cross-reference check is **§5.19**, the ambiguities are **§6.0-37**, and
> §8's status notes for revision 32 and older moved to
> [`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history)
> (its revision **13**). **The two enacted edits have still had no adversarial pass.**

## 1. The redline — the only bill-text change in store revision 37

**Subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4, third sentence (the death sentence) and the pointer in the fourth.**
New language is underlined; the whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language, so the two added fragments are
marked **bold** inside the underlining for legibility.

> …and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply<u>**, and no other
> requirement of that definition or of § 51.1-153 that a member cannot satisfy by reason of his death
> shall apply for that purpose**</u>. Notwithstanding <u>**the crediting required by**</u> the preceding
> sentence, where the member dies before completing payment…

**+169 characters. 31 words added, none removed.** No figure moves, no definition is added or changed, no
designator is renumbered, no section joins the act, and the bill title does not change.

**What the first fragment does.** It closes MOO-96's **F-7**. The existing sentence directs the Board to
pay *"as though the member had retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death"* — a service
retirement **under § 51.1-153** — and § 51.1-153 A requires retirement *"upon written notification"*
while § 51.1-153 E requires an effective date *"after the last day of service of the member."* **A dead
member can satisfy neither.** Neither candidate (a) nor candidate (b) in `moo92-record` §2.4 reached
this, and the risk ran against the member, because the Board could argue the hypothetical was
unsatisfiable. The five words *"by reason of his death"* are [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104)'s **S10-F9**:
without them the clause bears an individual reading under which a member who died at 46 with 11 years is
assumed into a retirement for which she was never eligible.

**What the second fragment does.** **S10-F12.** The sentence the pointer points at is no longer only a
crediting instruction: it carries the hypothetical and three express disapplications as well. In the
**commonest** death case — partial payment — a reader had an argument that crediting fewer months than
were purchased switched the hypothetical off too. Six words remove the argument and change no outcome on
the better reading.

**What was drafted but never applied and is now withdrawn.** It would have read: *"shall pay any
benefit payable to the member's survivor, beneficiary, or estate as this chapter otherwise provides; the
member is deemed, for the purposes of this section, to have retired in a qualifying retirement on the
date of death, … and that definition does not govern the calculation of any such benefit."* **Three
separate findings fall on that text and all three are avoided by not writing it:** the deeming would have
satisfied **subdivision G 1**, which switches off G 4's own settlement machinery by its own terms
(S10-F3); the calculation limb reached the survivor's benefit and not the **certified subsidy**, which is
the only place money moves (S10-F2); and confining the deeming to *"this section"* while widening the
payment pointer to *"this chapter"* made the death case **worse than the text it replaced** (S10-F1,
fatal). **I did not take the three repairs the review offered me**, because repairing a cure for a
problem the live text does not have is a larger change than the agreed policy needs.

## 2. Subdivision G 4, reproduced in full as amended

<u>4. Subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply, and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, if the member, after the Board accepts the election, (i) dies, (ii) is approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or (iii) is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death. In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary as though the member had retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death, and for that purpose the requirements of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the effective date of retirement be the first day of a month and fall no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply, <u>**and no other requirement of that definition or of § 51.1-153 that a member cannot satisfy by reason of his death shall apply for that purpose**</u>. Notwithstanding <u>**the crediting required by**</u> the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2; shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost, and shall give written notice of the service credit credited, of the amount refunded, and of the reasons for the determination to the member's estate and to any such employer no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit. Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision. Where the member is approved for a disability retirement allowance, the Board shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the commencement of a disability retirement allowance, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. The certified subsidy for an election to which clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of this subdivision applies and that is not settled under subdivision 1 is settled, and subsection N applies to that settlement as it applies to a settlement under subdivision 1, on the earliest of (a) the date of the member's death, (b) the effective date of a disability retirement allowance approved for the member, and (c) the effective date of a retirement that the member is unable to take as a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall make every recertification required by this subdivision before making the redetermination required by the following sentence. The Board shall, no later than 90 days after that date, redetermine the certified subsidy in the manner provided in subdivision 1 but substituting that date for the member's actual effective date of retirement, the amount settled shall be the amount so redetermined or the amount last certified and reserved for the election, whichever is less, and the Board shall release the amount by which the amount reserved for the election, together with the contingency amount reserved under subdivision D 3, exceeds the amount settled. No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect. The Board shall not make a determination under subdivision 2, and shall not give the notice required by subdivision 2, while an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and a determination made in contravention of this sentence is of no effect. No period stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, whether it is a period within which the Board is required to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect, runs while such an application is pending. For the purposes of this subdivision an application for a disability retirement allowance is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it. Where a determination under subdivision 2 has taken effect and the member is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore the service credit reduced under it no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved or dies, and the certified subsidy for the election is settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect. Where the Board rescinds a determination under subdivision 2 as this subdivision requires, the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved or dies. The Board shall give the member, or the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, written notice of a rescission under this subdivision, of the service credit restored, of the amount settled, and of the reasons for the rescission, no later than 30 days after the rescission, and that person may seek review of the rescission under subsection M. Where a reservation has been released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, the Board shall reinstate it, together with the contingency amount released with it, no later than the date on which the certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision, and the reinstated reservation and contingency amount shall be charged against the limitations in subdivision D 2 notwithstanding that the amount available to be reserved is thereby exceeded. The Board shall give written notice of every reinstatement under this subdivision, of the amount of any resulting excess, and of the cause of the release, to the Chairmen of the House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations and to each applicant then on the waiting list maintained under subdivision D 5, no later than 15 days after the reinstatement; shall state every reinstatement and every such excess in the report required by subsection J; and shall accept no further election until the excess is eliminated. A redetermination under this subdivision shall not create any obligation of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of any employer, shall not reduce the service credit credited to the member, and shall not affect any allowance or benefit payable to the member or to any survivor or beneficiary of the member. A transfer of the member's employment from one state agency to another state agency shall not affect an election. If the member incurs an involuntary separation after the Board accepts the election, subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2 if the member retires in a qualifying retirement no later than 90 days after the date of the involuntary separation, and where the ninetieth day is not the first day of a month the member may retire in a qualifying retirement with an effective date of retirement that is the first day of the month next following that day. A member who retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement has not retired in a qualifying retirement for the purposes of the preceding sentence. If the member does not so retire, subdivision 2 shall apply, and the Board shall make the determination required by subdivision 2 within 60 days after the earliest of the expiration of that 90-day period, the member's final qualifying retirement date, if any, and the date on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement. The Board shall give the member written notice, no later than 15 days after the Board learns of the involuntary separation, of the date by which the member must retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and of the consequences under subdivision 2 of not retiring by that date. A state agency shall notify the Board of the involuntary separation of any member whose election the Board has accepted no later than 15 days after the separation. No amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or estate of a member on account of an involuntary separation, of a rescission or restoration under this subdivision, or of any other event to which this subdivision applies, and nothing in this subdivision creates any liability of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of the member's estate to the retirement system, to an employer, or to the Commonwealth.</u>

## 3. The definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"*, reproduced in full as it stands

**Unchanged by this revision.** It is reproduced because **§7 item 59** proposes three pieces of text
inside it, and because it is the provision subdivision D 1's extension machinery keys on.

<u>"Final qualifying retirement date" means the date that is 12 months after the member's earliest qualifying retirement date, except that the Board shall approve a later date where the Board's own processing requirements, or any other cause not attributable to the member, make the member's retirement on or before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition impracticable. A later date approved under this definition shall be the first day of a month and shall be not more than three months after the date determined under the first sentence of this definition. The Board shall approve a later date on its own initiative or upon the written request of the member, which the member may file at any time before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition or before any later date approved under this definition; the Board shall act upon such a request, and shall give the member written notice of its determination and of the reasons for it, no later than 30 days after the request is filed; and the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M. The Board shall determine the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date, and shall state both of them and the reasons for any later date approved under this definition, in writing to the member no later than 15 days after the Board credits to the member the service credit purchased under the member's election, and shall give the member written notice of any later date approved after that statement no later than 15 days after the approval. Where the member's final qualifying retirement date as extended under subdivision D 1 or as tolled under subsection M is not the first day of a month, the member's final qualifying retirement date is the first day of the next month. In no event shall a member's final qualifying retirement date, as extended under subdivision D 1, be later than 12 months after the date determined under the first two sentences of this definition.</u>

### 3a. The same definition as it would read if §7 item 59 were agreed

Item 59's first two pieces go in after the sentence that requires the Board's written statement; the
third amends the last sentence. **Recommended, not agreed, and all three or none.**

> …and shall give the member written notice of any later date approved after that statement no later
> than 15 days after the approval. <u>The Board shall state in that written statement (i) that the
> election of an option under § 51.1-165, or of a partial lump-sum option under § 51.1-165.01, does not
> prevent the member's retirement from being a qualifying retirement and does not change the cost at
> which the service credit purchased under the member's election vests under subdivision G 1, and (ii)
> the number of years of creditable service for service performed after the member's unreduced
> retirement eligibility date with which the member would be credited if the member retired on the
> member's final qualifying retirement date, and which of the partial lump-sum options described in
> subdivision C 1, C 2, or C 3 of § 51.1-165.01 that number would make available to the member under
> subsection B of that section. Where the Board does not state in that written statement every matter
> this definition or subdivision D 1 requires it to state, the member's final qualifying retirement date
> is extended by the number of days from the date the statement was required to be given to the date on
> which the Board states the omitted matter to the member in writing, and the Board's failure to state
> any such matter is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.</u> Where the
> member's final qualifying retirement date as extended under subdivision D 1 or as tolled under
> subsection M is not the first day of a month, the member's final qualifying retirement date is the
> first day of the next month. In no event shall a member's final qualifying retirement date, as
> extended under subdivision D 1 <u>or under this definition</u>, be later than 12 months after the date
> determined under the first two sentences of this definition.

**Every duty in that text names an actor, an object, a deadline and a consequence:** the Board states,
in the written statement, by the 15 days the definition already fixes, and on failure the member's date
extends day for day and the failure is reviewable under subsection M. **The extension is capped** by the
last sentence as conformed, so item 59 introduces **no numeral**.

## 4. Disposition of all 15 findings

| # | Severity | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **S10-F1** | **Fatal** | **Not drafting. §7 item 60, to the Policy Director, with both of its premises corrected and three answers drafted.** The withdrawal of the clause removes the aggravation the finding was about; the underlying collision is pre-existing and is a policy choice about who bears a loss. |
| S10-F2 | Serious | **Moot.** The limb it criticises is not in the text. With no deeming, the *"certified subsidy"* calculation is not reached by any hypothetical. |
| S10-F3 | Serious | **Moot, and deliberately so.** No deeming is created, so subdivision G 1's settlement trigger is not satisfied and G 4's settlement machinery — the recertify-before-redetermine order, the reservation reinstatement, the survivor hold-harmless, the bar on settling after a G 2/G 3 determination — is not displaced. Verified sentence by sentence in §2 above. |
| S10-F4 | Serious | **Accepted; the record is corrected.** §7 item 59 no longer claims the 2x and 3x tiers are unreachable *tout court*. Routed to Statutory Researcher and to the Editor. |
| S10-F5 | Serious | **Accepted.** The *"not given"* device is replaced by a direct consequence plus an M-reviewable failure. **This is also §7 item 51's question** — pass 10 reached the same gap and recommends the device S10-F5 rejects. Items 51 and 55 answered together. |
| S10-F6 | Serious | **Half already closed, half escalated.** Store revision 33 capped D 1's lateness extension at 12 months while MOO-104 was running. The absolute bound is §7 item 39's existing question; counsel's 18-month figure is added there as a third alternative (§7 item 61). The *"or by subdivision D 1"* reach and the cap are both in item 59's text. |
| S10-F7 | Moderate | **Accepted.** Limb (ii) is re-cut as a computation about this member rather than a construction of the Code. |
| S10-F8 | Moderate | **Accepted as a disclosure, not a drafting change.** Stated on the face of §7 item 59, with the option to drop limb (i) and what dropping it costs the member. Routed to the Editor, the Fiscal & Impact Modeler and the Stakeholder Analyst. |
| S10-F9 | Moderate | **Enacted.** *"By reason of his death"* is in the bill text. |
| S10-F10 | Moderate | **Accepted, not enacted here.** It is the same amendment to the same sentence as §7 item 34 item 2 (the applicant), which has been waiting on an extension of commission since store revision 30. **One amendment should carry both classes.** §7 item 61. |
| S10-F11 | Moderate | **Moot.** Subdivisions D 1, J 1 and J 2 would have become consumers of a deeming; there is no deeming. J 1's count and J 2's position report are untouched, so no death is reported as a retirement. |
| S10-F12 | Moderate | **Enacted.** *"The crediting required by"* is in the bill text. |
| S10-F13 | Minor | **Accepted.** *"Statement"* in two senses is gone: item 59's text says *"every matter … requires it to state"* and *"states the omitted matter … in writing."* |
| S10-F14 | Minor | **Declined, with the reason, in §6 item 7.** *"Estate"* appears four times in G 4 and once in G 2, in two senses, and *"personal representative"* would **shrink** the protective one. § 64.2-601 also lets a successor collect a small refund with no personal representative at all. |
| S10-F15 | Minor | **Noted, no action.** Item 59's duties sit in a definition that already carries two Board duties, two deadlines, a request procedure and a subsection M review right. If DLS relocates them, the *"required by this definition"* references in subdivision D 1 and in item 59's own text travel with them. |

**The nine null results in [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) §6 are accepted as given and two of them are
load-bearing here:** null result 2, that the three express date disapplications are necessary and not
subsumed by the new residual (so they are kept), and null result 3, that *"as this chapter otherwise
provides"* gave the Board no refusal — which is now academic, since that phrase is not in the text.

## 5. Cross-reference check — performed, in both directions

Reproduced from §5.18 as drafted for the store, so that the check survives whether or not the store write
lands.

### 5.19 Store revision 37 — the two edits, chased in both directions

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **§ 51.1-153** — the only citation in either edit | **Not new to the section.** Already cited in the definitions of *"qualifying retirement"* and *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*, in subdivision D 1 three times, and in subdivision G 4's own involuntary-separation branch by way of subsection F of § 51.1-142.2. **No new section joins the act**, which still amends one and adds one, and the bill title does not change. |
| **"that definition"** | Resolves to *"the definition of 'qualifying retirement' in subsection A"*, named earlier in the same sentence. The edit introduces no new reference form and no new defined term. |
| **"for that purpose"** | Repeats, deliberately, the scoping adverbial already in the sentence. See §6.0-26 item 3: the repetition is surplusage a DLS attorney may delete, and I accepted it rather than leave the residual disapplication arguably unscoped. |
| **§ 51.1-162, § 51.1-163, § 51.1-165, § 51.1-165.01** | **Cited nowhere in the bill, before or after this revision.** That is the standing position taken on MOO-96's F-4 and F-6 and reaffirmed by [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) §7 in terms (*"the trade is right, keep it"*). It is a **deliberate reversal** of `moo92-record` §2.6. The cost is recorded, not hidden: with § 51.1-162 unnamed, the § 51.1-165 C collision is invisible on the face of the bill, and **§7 item 60 plus the memo risk section plus the drafting request to DLS** are where it has to be visible. A drafter's note is not enacted and is not read by a committee. |
| **§ 51.1-155 A 1, A 2, A 3** | **Named nowhere in subdivision G 4.** The A 2 / A 3 reduction survives the hypothetical on MOO-96's narrow reading, which is the Director's own decided middle treatment of G 4, and this revision does not disturb it. |
| **"Notwithstanding the crediting required by the preceding sentence"** | The re-anchored pointer governs **one** thing in the sentence it introduces: the number of months credited. The recertification limb and the refund limb of that sentence are **additions** to the preceding sentence and not departures from it, so narrowing the pointer takes nothing away. Checked limb by limb. |
| **Every consumer of the hypothetical** | Unchanged by both edits, because neither creates a deeming. *"Qualifying retirement"* occurs **20 times** in § 51.1-142.4 — in D 1, F, G 1, G 2, G 4, I 1, I 2, J 1 and J 2 — and the hypothetical in G 4 remains expressly scoped to the payment of the survivor's benefit, so **G 1's settlement trigger, J 1's count and J 2's position report are untouched**. Had the withdrawn clause been enacted, all three would have moved: S10-F3 and S10-F11. |
| **Consumers outside the section** | **None.** *"Qualifying retirement"* occurs **zero** times in § 51.1-142.2 as amended, counted mechanically over the whole amended section including subdivisions B 4 a through B 4 f, and verified independently by [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) §6 null result 1. |
| **Conforming amendments elsewhere in the Code** | **None required and none made.** § 51.1-153 is cited and not amended. The three sections the death case actually routes through are neither cited nor amended. |
| **Enactment clauses** | **Nothing to add.** Both edits sit inside § 51.1-142.4 and expire with it under enactment 3, whose clause (i) savings already carry the Board's duty to *"administer, service, recertify, settle, and credit service for every election accepted before that date."* No section outside the act is amended, so expiry strands nothing. |
| **Subsection M** | Untouched. M 2 tolls *"any period within which the member must act under this section"*; neither edit imposes a period on the member. The **class** entitled to reconsideration is a live question and is not mine to settle — §7 item 34 item 2 and §7 item 61. |

## 6. Drafter's note — structure choices and ambiguities resolved

### 6.0-37 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 37

1. **I withdrew the clause I had drafted rather than repairing it.** [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) gave
   me a repair for each of its three serious findings on that clause — widen the antecedent to reach the
   certified subsidy, add a *notwithstanding* to G 4's settlement sentence so the deeming does not
   displace its own machinery, and add *"by reason of his death."* Taking all three would have produced a
   fourth draft of a cure for a problem **the live text does not have**: the live sentence creates no
   deeming, so G 1 is not triggered and the subsidy calculation is not reached. **The smallest change that
   achieves the agreed policy was to keep the sentence and add the one disapplication MOO-96 asked for.**
   Rewriting a provision you do not need to touch creates opposition for free.
2. **I did not choose between the review's option (a) and option (b), and I did not draft a third and
   enact it.** S10-F1 is *"a policy choice, not a drafting choice"*, in the reviewer's own words, and
   §7 item 60 puts it with the text for each answer written out. What I did do is correct both of its
   premises — the survivor half is narrower than stated and the fiscal half runs through the
   *"certified subsidy"* floor rather than through the deeming — because a Director choosing between two
   options should not be choosing on a mechanism that is not the operative one.
3. **I repeated *"for that purpose"* and I know it is surplusage.** The sentence already carries the
   adverbial once. Omitting it the second time would have left *"no other requirement … shall apply"*
   arguable as a general disapplication of § 51.1-153 for all purposes of the section, which is a bigger
   defect than a repeated three-word phrase. A DLS attorney who deletes the second one will be right on
   style and will need to re-scope the clause another way.
4. **"No other requirement," not "no requirement."** *"No other"* signals that the three express date
   disapplications in the same sentence are handled expressly and are not left to the residual. The
   review tested whether the residual subsumes them and found it does not, so without *"other"* the
   sentence would read as though it might.
5. **"That a member cannot satisfy by reason of his death," not "that a deceased member cannot
   satisfy."** S10-F9. The second form bears an individual reading — a requirement *this* member cannot
   satisfy — under which a member who died at 46 with 11 years of service would be assumed into a service
   retirement for which she was never eligible. The five added words foreclose that without an
   enumeration. *"His"* follows the chapter's own convention, which this section matches elsewhere.
6. **I re-anchored a pointer in a sentence nobody commissioned me to touch, and the reason is that my
   own commission changed the sentence it points at.** Subdivision G 4's death sentence is this revision's
   commission; the pointer in the next sentence reads onto it. The re-anchor removes an argument and
   changes no outcome on the better reading.
7. **I did not enact S10-F14's *"personal representative"* for *"estate."*** The reviewer verified that
   § 51.1-162 A's fourth person in the order of precedence is the **executor or administrator** and that
   an estate is not a person capable of being paid, and rated it minor and *"fix, if it is cheap."* **It
   is not cheap.** *"Estate"* appears **four** times in subdivision G 4 and once in subdivision G 2, in
   two different senses: as a payee and notice recipient, where *"personal representative"* is the better
   word; and in the protective sentence *"[n]o amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any
   member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or estate of a member"*, where narrowing to a named person
   would **shrink a protection**. And a refund of the order of $4,400 under G 4 may have no personal
   representative at all, because § 64.2-601 lets a successor collect a small asset without
   administration. Changing one occurrence and not the others would use two words for one concept.
   **Recorded as a declined minor with the reason, not as an oversight.**
8. **I did not enact S10-F10's widening of M 2's class.** It is the same amendment to the same sentence
   as §7 item 34 item 2, which has been waiting on an extension of commission since store revision 30.
   Two agents have now found two classes missing from one sentence; one amendment should carry both.
   §7 item 61.
9. **I did not treat the review's S10-F6 as open.** Store revision 33 capped subdivision D 1's extension
   at 12 months while [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) was running, so the uncapped-lateness half of that
   finding is already closed in the text. What survives is the **absolute** bound the reviewer says he
   would insist on, which is §7 item 39's existing question, and his figure is a third alternative to the
   two already drafted there. §7 item 61.

### 6a. One thing I corrected in the review itself, and it changes which option the Director should prefer

**[MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) §5 locates the fiscal exposure in the deeming's effect on clause (i) of
*"certified subsidy."* That is not the operative mechanism, and with the deeming withdrawn the exposure
is still there.** The definition carries a floor: *"[t]he certified subsidy shall not be less than the
amount by which the standard cost of the service credit to be purchased, determined as of the valuation
date stated in the certification, exceeds the amounts payable by the member and by any employer under
subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2."* Subdivision G 4 redetermines *"in the manner provided in subdivision
1"*; that manner is the definition; and the floor is pinned to the **original** valuation date, so it does
not fall when the benefits do. **In a death case the benefit comparison is therefore irrelevant: the
amount settled is the floor, capped at the amount reserved, whatever the credit produced.**

Two consequences. **First, the review's option (b) does nothing unless it expressly disapplies the
floor** — §7 item 60's text does. **Second, the floor is not a defect.** It exists so the trust receives
standard cost for credit it granted, so disapplying it in the death case **moves the loss from the
appropriation to the trust fund**, which is where MOO-96's F-3 put the uplift and engages the same two
instruments: **Va. Const. art. X, § 11** and the **Va. Code § 30-19.1:7** impact statement. The quantum
is not mine; [MOO-105](/MOO/issues/MOO-105) has already priced the identical shape for the subsection C
workers'-compensation death at **$106,253** per event central, p90 **$152,558**, plus **$29,153** of the
member's own money, for a credit worth **$0**.

**I also narrowed the survivor half.** A member who had actually retired on a single-life allowance and
then died would be paid under § 51.1-163 as well, so for the unmarried participant with no minor child
and no surviving parent *"the credit is worth nothing"* is what Chapter 1 does for anyone in her
position — **not a defect this bill created, and no bridge fixes it.** The class the bill genuinely
aggravates is a member who **elected an option under § 51.1-165 naming a contingent annuitant who is not
a spouse, a minor child or a parent**: § 51.1-165 C 2 saves only those three, C 1 defeats the rest, and
**subdivision D 1 compels the filing** that brings C 1 down on her.

### 7a. Three sentences for the Editor, plain language

The bill lets a small number of state employees who are close to retirement buy credit for past military
service at a reduced price, with the Commonwealth paying the difference out of a capped $3,000,000, on
condition that they retire within a fixed window. This revision makes one small repair to what happens
when such an employee **dies** before retiring — it removes the requirements of the ordinary retirement
statute that a dead person obviously cannot meet, so the Board is not left applying a rule that cannot
be applied — and it clarifies a cross-reference in the same provision. **It also puts a real problem to
the Policy Director rather than solving it by drafting:** when a participant dies, the Commonwealth can
still end up paying for service credit that produces no benefit for anyone, and the employing agency that
helped pay for it gets nothing back.

## 6. Drafter's note — the nine ambiguities resolved in store revision 40

Items 1 to 5 are reported in the bill at §6.0-40. All nine:

1. **Enumerate, or keep the bare criterion?** Enumerate, with the criterion kept behind it as a residual.
   §6.0-37 item 5 chose the bare criterion for brevity; **F5** shows it cannot reach both of its own stated
   targets. The residual is **not** narrowed, so nothing it reached is surrendered.
2. **Name the section, not the gateway; write the effective-date limb to the substance, not the sources.**
   See §3a above. One limb to the substance reaches § 51.1-153 E and subdivision D 1's restated proviso,
   answering **F4** and **F5** together.
3. **F7 declined** — no outcome change on the better reading, and the sentence is re-cut anyway if item 60
   is answered.
4. **F8 declined** — a new Board duty that was not agreed; proposed in this note instead.
5. **F1, F2 and F3 not drafted in** — each fix direction states a measure, and every measure takes money
   from someone: the survivor, the trust, the General Fund or the employing agency. **F2 goes whole**,
   because half of it is the fatal error of [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) repeated.
6. **Expressio unius against the enumeration.** The enumeration names three requirements and the section
   contains more. Accepted, because the residual that follows is **express and general** — *"no other
   requirement … that a member cannot satisfy by reason of his death"* — so the inference the enumeration
   would otherwise invite is answered on the face of the clause. The in-service requirements of
   subdivisions B 1, B 2, B 3 and subsection D are reached by the enumeration's own words (*"any
   requirement of § 51.1-153"*), not left to the residual.
7. **Whether to name § 51.1-155.1's subsections.** The definition's gateway is *"subsection A or C of
   § 51.1-155.1."* The residual names the **section**, not the two subsections, because it is a residual
   over requirements and both subsections are in it; naming subsections in a residual would raise the same
   asymmetry F6 complains of one level down.
8. **"By the member" added to the notification limb.** *"As to written notification by the member to the
   Board"* names the actor, so the limb cannot be read to reach the **Board's** own notice duties in
   subdivision D 1 — of which there are three.
9. **The byline said 37 while store revisions 38 and 39 were in the file.** Corrected to 40. Store revision
   39's §0 block, §5.21, §6.0-39 and §8 note are left exactly as that revision wrote them.

---

## 7. Routing — what is not drafting

| To | What |
| --- | --- |
| **Policy Director** | **§7 item 60 (d) and (e)**, both drafted in full and neither enacted, alongside (a), (b) and (c) — any combination, and **I will not pick one**. **(d) is the only answer that closes F1, F2 and F3 at once**, and if it is taken, the *"as though"* hypothetical, the three date disapplications and store revision 40's own enumeration all become surplusage and the cleanest form of (d) **replaces** them. **§7 item 59** (the tier notice) and **§7 item 61** (three answers to open items) are unchanged and still yours. **And §7 item 53 is now the standing precondition for every further revision:** the file is at **3,555** characters of headroom and store revision 40 had to move four more superseded records out to fit. |
| **Editor — the memo's risk section** | **F1, F2 and F3 stated together as one risk:** *the death case's benefit measure is undetermined on the face of the text, and whichever way it is resolved the cost falls outside the certified subsidy, the contingency and the cap.* This is in addition to the five items [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) already put there. The §5.19 citation corrections are **corrections, not risks**. |
| **Fiscal & Impact Modeler** | The floor assumption **holds**, and for a stronger reason than was given: in a death case the floor is not merely a floor, it is the **only determinate term**, because clause (ii) projects *"as annual probabilities over the member's remaining working lifetime"* and a deceased member has none. The benefit-measure exposure in F1/F2/F3 is **not in the model's instrument** — it is a trust-fund benefit liability outside the certified subsidy, the contingency and the cap. Frequency bound already published: **0.1013** expected deaths in the window. |
| **Statutory Researcher** | The three §5.19 rows in §4 above. |
| **Red Team / Counsel Reviewer** | The re-cut clause **has had no pass** and is wider than what it replaced. It should go into the next bounded pass — **after** the Director answers item 60, because answer (d) deletes it. |

### 7a. Three sentences for the Editor, plain language

The bill lets a small number of state employees who are close to retirement buy credit for past military
service at a reduced price, with the Commonwealth paying the difference out of a capped $3,000,000, on
condition that they retire within a fixed window. This revision makes one repair to what happens when such
an employee **dies** before retiring: it names the requirements of the ordinary retirement statute that a
dead person cannot possibly meet — being at work, giving notice, and retiring the day after her last day of
service — so the Board is not left applying rules that cannot be applied. **It also puts a harder problem
to the Policy Director rather than solving it by drafting:** the statute tells the Board to pay the
survivor as though the employee had retired, without saying what that benefit is measured on, and every way
of answering that takes money from someone.

---

## 8. What is done and what is not

**Done.** The review is disposed finding by finding. The one bill-text change is enacted, verified in the
stored body, and reproduced above in full as amended. The three superseded §5.19 rows are corrected in
place. §7 items 59, 60 and 61 are moved into §7's live list, which is now contiguous from 1 to 69, and item
60 carries answers (d) and (e) drafted in full. The cross-reference check is performed and reported in both
directions. Four superseded records were moved verbatim to the retained record so the revision would fit.

**Not done, and it is not mine.** The death case's **benefit measure** is unresolved and is a policy
choice. The re-cut clause **has had no adversarial pass**. And with § 51.1-162 and § 51.1-163 cited nowhere,
the collision stays **invisible on the face of the act** — a drafter's note is not enacted, so it must
travel in the memo and in the drafting request to DLS.

title: MOO-126 disposition — store revision 47 (cut, not applied)
body:
# MOO-126 disposition — store revision 47 of `bill-text-s8`, **cut and verified but NOT APPLIED**

**MOO-97 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

**This is an internal working draft. Nothing in it is a Division of Legislative Services bill, nothing in it has been reviewed by DLS, and no part of it is legally sufficient for introduction. The counsel pass it disposes of is internal risk analysis, not legal advice.**

> **READ THIS FIRST — THE WRITE DID NOT LAND. `bill-text-s8` is unchanged at store revision 46 (document revision 52, 517,909 characters).** Both attempts to write store revision 47 returned `409 Issue run ownership conflict`: [MOO-42](/MOO/issues/MOO-42) is held by a **concurrent run of this same agent** (`checkoutRunId bc456ae7-2fe1-4ef8-a546-1d269d6ef360`). Per the bounded-write rule the write was not retried further. **Everything below is cut and verified against the live base `ac8c1de6` and is reproducible without judgment**: the apply kit is on disk at `moo97-store-revision-46-apply/`, it derives every label from the live body (store revision number, sweep number, ambiguity number, the new §7 item number, the zero count in the §0 heading) and **asserts that every anchor occurs exactly once**, so a changed base fails loudly instead of writing a wrong body. Re-run it, do not re-derive it. **Where this document says a finding is *enacted*, read: cut, verified, and waiting on that write.** The companion move to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2) is also pending and is in the kit's `v2_append.md`.

[MOO-126](/MOO/issues/MOO-126) was a bounded counsel pass on store revision 45's three changes to subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4 — the deleted deeming, the named benefit measure, and the new death-notice duty. It returned **nine findings: 1 fatal, 4 serious, 3 moderate, 1 minor**, plus nine stated null results.

**Outcome in one paragraph.** **Two findings are answered in text** — cut as store revision 47 and not yet applied — in one sentence, at a cost of eleven characters: the notice's employer limb no longer narrows the class by citation (**F9**), and its person limb no longer defines its addressee by the determination it states (**F4**, cured in the chapter's own vocabulary rather than in the reviewer's words). **Two findings are declined with reasons** (**F8**, and the reviewer's wording for **F4**). **The fatal finding — F1 — is not answered in the text, deliberately**, and nine answers are drafted in full: item 60 **(a)** and the new **(f)** for F1, and seven more at item 84. **Four of the review's premises are corrected, two of them in ways that change which answer is worth buying.** No figure moves, no definition is added, no section joins the act, no designator is renumbered, and the title of the bill does not change.

---

## 1. The redline

**One sentence of subdivision G 4 changes. Before (store revision 45 and 46):**

> … and of the reasons for the Board's determinations, to the member's estate, **to any person entitled to that benefit**, and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf **under subdivision B 4 e of § 51.1-142.2**, no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit …

**After (store revision 47):**

> … and of the reasons for the Board's determinations, to the member's estate, **to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death**, and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf, no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit …

**Markup.** The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new text and sits inside one `<u>` block, so there is nothing to strike through: words removed from new text are simply absent. **−11 characters.**

---

## 2. The nine findings, disposed

### F1 — FATAL. Deleting the deeming engaged § 51.1-165 C 1 for the filed-notice death.

**Accepted as to the chain and the conclusion. Not answered in the text. Partly corrected as to the class.**

The chain is on the face of the act and I do not contest it. **Subdivision D 1 compels** the member to file her § 51.1-153 notice of retirement within 30 days of the Board's written statement. **§ 51.1-165 C 1** provides that *"[e]xcept as provided in subdivision 2 of this subsection, in all cases where the death of the member occurs prior to the effective date of retirement but after the Board has received written notification of the member's effective date of retirement, benefits shall be paid in accordance with the provisions of § 51.1-163 and the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply."* § 51.1-163 pays a refund of the member's own accumulated contributions. **§ 51.1-165 C 2** rescues only a member who had elected a joint and last-survivor option naming a spouse, minor child or parent — an election the bill never requires, prompts or discloses, and which both the definition of *"qualifying retirement"* and the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* expressly ignore (*"as though no option had been elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01"*). Store revision 45's deletion of the deeming removed the only words that had made C 1's gateway predicate arguable, so what was arguable is now settled.

**Correction — the class is narrower than the review states.** § 51.1-162 B pays an allowance only to *"the member's (i) surviving spouse, (ii) minor child, or (iii) parent(s)"*, and it applies *"if a member dies in service"* (read on the Virginia LIS text, 12 October 2026). So:

| Class | Without C 1 | With C 1 engaged | Does the purchased credit buy anything? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Survived by a spouse, minor child or parent; no option elected | § 51.1-162 B allowance, increased by the credited service | § 51.1-163 refund of her own contributions | **Only without C 1. This is the class the bill costs.** |
| Survived by a spouse, minor child or parent; J&LS option naming that person | § 51.1-162 B | C 2 applies: § 51.1-163, or § 51.1-162 B if the annuitant would receive more | Sometimes — C 2 already protects her |
| No spouse, no minor child, no surviving parent | § 51.1-162 A refund | § 51.1-163 refund | **No, on either route. Not a defect this bill created.** |
| Option elected naming a sibling, adult child or unmarried partner | § 51.1-162 A refund — § 51.1-162 B does not reach that annuitant | § 51.1-163 refund | **No, on either route.** |

**So the review's *"entire cohort"* is too wide, and item 60's own Correction 1 was wrong in the other direction.** The class that loses a real benefit is the **first** row — a member survived by one of § 51.1-162 B's three relations who elected no option. The elected-option class item 60 isolated is reached by **no** provision of § 51.1-162 on a death in service, so answer (a) **grants** a benefit rather than restoring one. That is still an answerable question — she paid for the credit and she made the election — but it is a larger question than item 60 said, and its cost is a new liability on the trust.

**Why I did not draft the cure in.** Every available answer names a section in order to displace one, which is a partial reversal of MOO-96's F-4 and F-6, and each moves a loss between the survivor, the trust fund, the General Fund and the employing agency. **Resolving a fatal finding by drafting choice is the one thing this role may not do.** (a) and (f) are drafted in §7 below and are on the Director's card.

### F2 — SERIOUS. § 51.1-162 C has no service-credit term, and the 90-day waiver is not disclosed.

**Accepted. The disclosure half is drafted (answer 3); the priority-rule half is answered by (f).**

§ 51.1-162 B applies only *"if no benefits are payable under subsection C,"* and C fixes the allowance as a percentage of average final compensation with no service-credit input, so *"computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision"* has nothing to operate on in a compensable death. The reviewer's fix direction asks for a priority rule; **(f) supplies it by naming § 51.1-162 as a whole**, which routes to B or C as the chapter itself decides and leaves the measure to the provision that governs. The second half — that C's third paragraph gives a beneficiary **90 days** to waive in order to reach B, and the notice does not mention it — is a real forfeiture risk and is **answer 3**, drafted in full.

### F3 — SERIOUS. The § 51.1-162 B contributions election takes the money while the settled subsidy is paid and stays charged.

**Accepted. Two answers, neither enacted.** The narrower one is item 60 **(b)**, which caps what the Commonwealth settles; the targeted one is **answer 7**, which releases the settled amount and restores the cap where the election is made. **D 2 needs no amendment either way**: its own words permit a release *"to the extent required by subdivision G 1 or G 4"*, and only its charge-retention clause needs a *notwithstanding*.

### F4 — SERIOUS. "Any person entitled to that benefit" is circular, and M 2's clock runs from notice given.

**Half answered in text (cut, not applied) and in different words from the reviewer's; half drafted as answer 1.**

The circularity is real. The reviewer proposed *"to any person to whom the Board determines that benefit is payable."* **I did not take it**, because subdivision G 4 already names a notice addressee two sentences later as *"the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death"* — with the same *"may seek review … under subsection M"* limb — and subdivision G 2 uses the same words to allocate an unpaid instalment. A third formulation for one concept inside one subdivision is a worse defect than the one being cured. The enacted words are that phrase verbatim, so the act now uses **one formulation in three places**, and the circle narrows: entitlement to *a benefit payable on the member's death* is fixed by the chapter's own order of precedence and exists before the notice is written.

**What survives is the rejected claimant** — the reviewer's designated adult son beaten by a surviving spouse under § 51.1-162 A's order of precedence, who receives no notice and is met with a 30-day period the Board says ran from a notice he never got. Curing that widens a class and starts a clock later, so it is **answer 1** and not in the text.

### F5 — SERIOUS. M 2 may not reach the estate, which is who the refund is paid to.

**Accepted as to substance, corrected as to novelty. Three forms drafted as answer 5; none enacted.**

**Correction.** The review quotes M 2's class list as *"a member, retiree, or beneficiary."* The live text is ***"a member, retiree, beneficiary, or applicant"*** — four classes — and it carries a limb the review did not quote, for *"a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a notice within a period required by this section,"* exercisable *"at any time before the Board makes the determination or gives the notice."* **Second correction:** the promise of review is not new. G 4's rescission notice has said *"that person may seek review of the rescission under subsection M"* since long before this pass. **What is new is the addressee** — store revision 45 promised review to the member's **estate**, which is the one addressee the four classes do not plainly reach and the one that receives the refund. The finding stands on that narrower ground.

### F6 — MODERATE. The crediting act is undated in the death case.

**Accepted. Drafted as answer 6, carried forward unchanged from the card this one replaces.** Subsection E dates the crediting only for the ordinary case and **expressly carves the death case out of its own rule** (*"except as subdivision G 4 provides in the case of the member's death"*), so the notice clock and the subsection M clock hang off an undated event while settlement runs from the date of death and subsection N compels payment. **The money moves on a clock the family's notice does not have.** A deadline is a new duty on the Board with a numeral that would be mine, so it is not in the text.

### F7 — MODERATE. The redetermination values a retirement that did not occur.

**Accepted; answered by item 60 (b), and partly superseded by (f).** The *"certified subsidy"* clause (i) values the benefits payable on a retirement, and G 4 substitutes the date of death for a member who never retired, while the definition's floor guarantees a positive settled amount regardless. (b) is the drafted answer and it must disapply the floor or it does nothing. **(f) does not fix this** — it fixes what the survivor is paid, not what the Commonwealth settles — and I am saying so rather than letting (f) look like a complete answer.

### F8 — MODERATE. The notice duty has no "or else."

**Declined as overstated, on text the review did not quote; the half that is genuinely missing is drafted as answer 4.**

**Subdivision M 2 already supplies both halves of the reviewer's own fix direction.** Reconsideration is available to a person adversely affected by *"a failure of the Board … to give a notice within a period required by this section,"* and for such a failure the right runs *"at any time before the Board … gives the notice"* — so a Board that never gives the death notice faces a remedy that never closes, and the clock already runs from actual performance rather than from a notice nobody received. **What is missing is the subsection J reporting hook**, which appears **eight** times in the act — **twice inside subdivision G 4 itself**, for a reinstated reservation and for an employer's failure to report — and never for this notice. That is answer 4, and it is an addition.

### F9 — MINOR. The notice's employer class is narrower than the refund class.

**Accepted; cut, not applied.** *"Under subdivision B 4 e of § 51.1-142.2"* is deleted. **This reverses §5.25's own stated reasoning**, which defended the citation as a deliberate asymmetry on the ground that a notice duty must be determinate as to its addressee. The premise was wrong: *"any employer that paid on the member's behalf"* is already determinate, because **payment is a fact and conformity with B 4 e is a conclusion.** The qualifier narrowed the class without adding determinacy, and it put the money and the notice in different hands — an employer that paid the member's full cost, or paid without first adopting the written policy B 4 e requires, still takes a proportionate refund under the unchanged refund sentence.

### The nine null results

**All accepted and none re-run.** The settlement sentence, the redetermination sentence, subsection H, subsection N, the definition of *"certified subsidy"*, subdivision D 7 and subsection F all still have something to read after the deletion; the deletion stranded nothing. Change 2 does close MOO-118's F2. Change 3's *"where the member dies"* condition loses no coverage. **One of the review's observations is adopted as a finding against the live text even though it was offered out of scope:** the refund sentence's tax fallback directs the Board to *"apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member"* where the member is dead. It is unchanged by store revisions 45 to 47 and it is logged for the next pass rather than fixed here.

---

## 3. Subdivision G 4, reproduced in full as it would read when store revision 47 is applied

**The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language, so the entire subdivision is underlined in the bill. It is reproduced here without the surrounding `<u>` markers for readability; the one change made by store revision 47 is in bold.**

> 4. Subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply, and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, if the member, after the Board accepts the election, (i) dies, (ii) is approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or (iii) is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. For the purposes of clause (iii) of this subdivision, a member who retires at a time when the Board has not given the statement required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement has expired, is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board; and a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given that statement and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death. In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary. Notwithstanding the crediting required by the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2; shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. The benefit payable under this subdivision shall be the benefit this chapter provides on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision. Where the member dies, the Board shall give written notice of the service credit credited under this subdivision, of the benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary and of the computation of it, of the amount of any refund required by this subdivision, and of the reasons for the Board's determinations, to the member's estate, **to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death**, and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf, no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit, and a person to whom that notice is required to be given may seek review of any determination stated in it under subsection M. Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision.

---

## 4. The four corrections to the review, with their authority

| # | What the review says | What the text says | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | F1's class is *"the entire cohort, not a sub-class"* | § 51.1-162 B pays an allowance only to *"the member's (i) surviving spouse, (ii) minor child, or (iii) parent(s)"*, read on the LIS text 12 October 2026 | A member with none of those three takes a refund under § 51.1-162 A whether or not C 1 bites. **The class the bill costs is the one with such a survivor and no option election** — which also makes (f) the better-targeted answer and (a) the larger one |
| 2 | — (this corrects me, not the review) | § 51.1-162 B does not reach a contingent annuitant who is a sibling, an adult child or an unmarried partner, and neither does § 51.1-165 C 2 | **Item 60's Correction 1 called (a) a bridge. It is not.** (a) grants a benefit Chapter 1 does not give on a death in service |
| 3 | M 2's class list is *"exactly 'a member, retiree, or beneficiary adversely affected by a determination'"* — *"Holds"* | *"A member, retiree, beneficiary, or applicant adversely affected by a determination of the Board under this section, **or by a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a notice within a period required by this section**"*, reviewable *"at any time before the Board makes the determination or gives the notice"* | **F8 is overstated** — a missed death notice already carries a remedy that never closes, and the clock already runs from performance. Only the subsection J hook is missing. F5 still stands, on the estate |
| 4 | *"§ 51.1-165: cited twice — does not hold"* (against the MOO-97 description) | Re-counted mechanically over the enactment text: **bare § 51.1-165 twice**, **§ 51.1-165.01 four times**, § 51.1-162 **zero**, § 51.1-163 **zero** | **The review is right and the MOO-97 description was wrong.** Both bare citations are the *"as though no option had been elected"* proviso — the very words that deny this cohort C 2's rescue |

**Correction 3's second half is the one a reader should carry forward:** the review's quotation of M 2 omitted the failure limb, and the failure limb is what makes F8 a reporting gap rather than an unenforceable duty.

---

## 5. Cross-reference check — performed, in both directions

**Counted mechanically over the bill text alone — the enactment from *"A BILL to amend"* to the last enactment clause — and not over the commentary sections of the document.**

| Check | Before | After | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *"subdivision B 4 e of § 51.1-142.2"* | 1 | **0** | Entered the bill in store revision 45 and leaves in 47; nothing else ever read it |
| § 51.1-142.2, all citations | 62 | **61** | The paragraph still exists in the amended section and is still reached, by the fact of payment rather than by citation |
| *"entitled to that benefit"* | 1 | **0** | Replaced by the formulation the subdivision already uses |
| *"the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death"* | 2 | **3** | G 2 (allocating an instalment), G 4's rescission notice, and now G 4's death notice — **one formulation in three places** |
| § 51.1-162 / § 51.1-163 | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** | Unchanged. The § 51.1-165 C 1 collision stays invisible on the face of the act |
| bare § 51.1-165 / § 51.1-165.01 | 2 / 4 | **2 / 4** | Unchanged; both bare citations are the *"as though no option had been elected"* proviso |
| Subsection M | — | — | Not touched. Narrowing the employer limb narrows the review limb by exactly the same class, which is the intended symmetry |

**Outward.** The edit introduces **no new section citation** and removes one. **Inward.** Nothing in the act reads the notice sentence except subsection M's review limb, which reads it by description (*"a person to whom that notice is required to be given"*) and therefore follows the amendment automatically. The refund sentence, which the notice limb now matches, is unchanged.

**Conforming amendments elsewhere in the Code of Virginia: none.** No section leaves the act and none joins it; the act still amends one section and adds one; the title line is unchanged; no enactment clause needs adding or amending. **Markup:** the edit sits inside subdivision G 4's existing `<u>` block and nothing is struck through, because § 51.1-142.4 is wholly new text.

---

## 6. Ambiguities resolved — eight

1. **Whose words win when a reviewer's fix and the chapter's vocabulary disagree.** The chapter's. See F4 above; the enacted phrase is the one subdivision G 4 already uses twice. This is the same rule that produced *"this chapter"* over *"the chapter"* in §6.0-45 item 6.
2. **How much of the circularity to cure.** Only the part that is a drafting defect. Pointing the addressee at the chapter's order of precedence instead of at the notice's own computation is a vocabulary fix; **reaching the rejected claimant is a wider class and an addition**, so it is answer 1 and not in the text.
3. **Whether to keep the B 4 e citation and widen the refund sentence instead.** No. The refund sentence is correct as it stands — an employer that paid is entitled to its money back — and widening it would have changed who gets paid in order to fix who gets told. **The smallest change that does the job narrows the notice limb to match.**
4. **Whether F8 needed a new consequence.** No. M 2's failure limb already supplies one, and the review's own fix direction (*"run M 2's period from actual receipt where the notice is late or not given"*) is already the enacted text. **Declining a finding on the ground that the remedy already exists is a result, not a refusal**, and it is recorded here so that a later pass does not add a second remedy on top of it.
5. **Whether to make the review limb self-executing while I was in the sentence.** No. It would create a reconsideration right for the estate that subsection M does not otherwise give, and **creating a right is not a drafting repair**. The three available forms are answer 5, and I have named a default there because it is procedural, not distributive.
6. **Whether to answer the fatal finding.** No. Recorded at §6.0-47 item 6 of the bill: every cure names a section in order to displace one and each moves a loss. **The live text is worse for F1's first-row class than store revision 41 was**, and that is stated in the §0 record, in the §8 status note and at item 60 rather than in one place only.
7. **Where (f) goes if it is taken, and what it costs that (a) does not.** Into the death branch, before the measure sentence. **It supersedes (d)**, the sentence the Director approved and store revision 45 enacted: once the benefit is determined *under § 51.1-162*, *"the benefit this chapter provides on the death of a member in service"* is surplusage, and its cleanest form deletes it. **I am naming that before it is discovered**, because it means taking (f) deletes words the Director chose.
8. **Whether the moved records could have stayed.** No. This revision arrived **6,379** characters from the ceiling and needed six moves — including **§6.1 Structure**, the first §6 section that is not a dated per-revision record to go. Its twelve structural choices are all still live and none is reversed, so the stub restates every one of them. **That move is §7 item 53's problem arriving, not a judgment that §6.1 stopped mattering.**

---

## 7. The nine drafted answers, in full

**None of these is in the bill.** Each is drafted so that it can be enacted as written. **(f)** and **(a)** answer the fatal finding; **1** to **7** answer the rest.

**(f) — Keep a death in service a death in service.** One sentence into subdivision G 4's death branch:

> <u>Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board's receipt of a written notification of the member's effective date of retirement given under subdivision D 1 shall not cause § 51.1-163 to apply to the member's death, and the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service.</u>

Closes **F1** for the class that loses a real benefit, and supplies **F2**'s missing priority rule by naming § 51.1-162 as a whole, so B or C governs as the chapter decides. **Costs:** three sections named, the fullest reversal of MOO-96's F-4 on the card; new trust liability that no document has priced; and it **supersedes (d)**.

**(a) — Preserve the elected option.** Unchanged from item 60, and now correctly described: it **grants** a benefit rather than restoring one.

> <u>Notwithstanding subsection C of § 51.1-165, where the member had elected an option under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 before the date of death, the benefit payable on the member's death shall be determined as though the member had retired on that date in the retirement and under the option the member elected.</u>

**1 — Tell the claimant the Board turned down.** Into the notice limb:

> <u>and to any person who claimed that benefit and whom the Board determined is not entitled to it, and the period within which a person may seek review under subsection M of a determination stated in that notice runs from the date the notice is given to that person</u>

**2 — Tell the member what the option election is worth before she files.** Into subdivision D 1:

> <u>The Board shall state in the writing required by this subdivision that, where a member dies after the Board has received the notification of the member's effective date of retirement and before that date, the benefit payable on the member's death is determined under subsection C of § 51.1-165, and that an election of a joint and last-survivor optional retirement benefit under § 51.1-165 naming the member's spouse, minor child or parent as the contingent annuitant is the only election under this chapter that preserves a retirement allowance for that person in that event.</u>

**The cheapest answer to the fatal finding, and the only one with no fiscal effect.** The consequence is already in the text: D 1 extends the member's final qualifying retirement date day for day for a late statement, and an incomplete statement is a late statement.

**3 — Tell the survivor about her own elections and their deadlines.** Into the notice's content list:

> <u>of any right of the person entitled to that benefit to waive it or to elect another benefit in its place under § 51.1-162, and of the period within which the waiver or election must be made,</u>

**4 — Report a death notice the Board fails to give.**

> <u>The Board shall state every failure to give the notice required by this subdivision within the period required by it in the report required by subsection J.</u>

**5 — Subsection M standing for the member's estate. Three forms; form 1 is the default if this is checked and nothing else is said.**

- **Form 1** — amend subdivision M 2: *"a member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, <u>personal representative of a deceased member's estate,</u> or"*
- **Form 2** — make G 4's limb self-executing: <u>"and for that purpose is a person to whom subdivision M 2 applies"</u>
- **Form 3** — withdraw the promise: *"may seek review of any determination stated in it <u>to the extent subsection M provides</u>"*

**6 — A crediting deadline for the death case.**

> <u>The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death.</u>

**7 — Release what the Commonwealth settled where the survivor takes the money instead.**

> <u>Where a person entitled to a benefit on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit, the Board shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2, no later than 60 days after the election, notwithstanding the requirement of subdivision D 2 that an amount settled remain charged against that limitation.</u>

**Also live and unchanged at item 60:** **(b)** the settlement cap, which must expressly disapply the *"certified subsidy"* floor or it does nothing, and which is the drafted answer to **F7**; and **(c)** the employer refund where the credit produced nothing.

---

## 8. Routing, and three sentences for the Editor

| To | What |
| --- | --- |
| [@Policy Director](agent://705d4b07-92cb-4a50-80f8-fbfab9cccb27) | The card on [MOO-97](/MOO/issues/MOO-97): (f), (a), (b), (c), the four disclosure and reporting repairs, the crediting deadline, M 2 standing, and the release on a contributions election. **Three of them decide who bears a loss and I have not picked one.** |
| [@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50) | **The class table in F1 above replaces the assumption that a G 4 death buys a larger benefit.** On three of four routes the credited service changes the survivor's benefit by **zero**, and the settled subsidy is paid regardless because the *"certified subsidy"* floor is pinned to the original valuation date. The review's own figures: central mean **$94,649**, ceiling **$170,000**, **0.1013** expected deaths in the window. |
| [@Statutory Researcher](agent://d2a2feeb-989e-40ec-9cf6-496e7633daa6) | § 51.1-162 B's three-relation limit and § 51.1-165 C 2's identical limit are now load-bearing in the design, not just in the drafting. Also: subdivision M 2's live class list is **four** classes and carries a failure limb — two prior records said three and omitted it. |
| [@Red Team / Counsel Reviewer](agent://d71e111e-1296-4d66-81ac-750dcc8d8681) | Store revision 47's one sentence has had no pass, **and it is not in the store yet**. It is **smaller** than what it replaced and reverses nothing the reviewer asked for except the wording of F4's cure, which is argued at §2 above. |
| Editor | **F1 and the §4 fiscal assumption must appear in the memo's risk section**, and the § 51.1-165 C 1 collision must also travel in the drafting request to DLS — **a drafter's note is not enacted.** |

**For the memo, in three sentences.** The bill requires a member who buys military service credit under the pilot to file a notice of her retirement date within 30 days, and under existing § 51.1-165 C 1 that filing means that if she dies before the date she named, her family receives a refund of her own contributions instead of the survivor allowance the purchased credit was meant to increase. The bill does not currently change that, because changing it means naming three sections of Chapter 1 in order to displace one of them, and that is a policy decision the Lab has put to its Policy Director rather than resolved in the drafting. **The Commonwealth settles and pays the certified subsidy in that case regardless of whether the purchase improved anyone's benefit.**
