title: MOO-154 disposition — store revision 58: 16 findings disposed, 8 substitutions enacted, 9 answers drafted
body:
# MOO-154 disposition — store revision 58 of `bill-text-s8`

**MOO-97 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

**Internal working draft throughout. Nothing here is a Division of Legislative Services bill, nothing in it has been reviewed by DLS, and no part of it is legally sufficient for introduction. Every figure and every option below is pre-decisional.**

[MOO-154](/MOO/issues/MOO-154) returned **16 findings — 1 fatal (F1), 8 serious (F2 to F9), 5 moderate (F10 to F13, F15) and 2 minor (F14, F16)** — plus 12 stated null results and 13 re-checked citations, on the seven edits the Policy Director's card of 12 October put into subdivisions G 4, D 1 and M 2 of new § 51.1-142.4.

**Eleven findings are answered in the text as store revision 58. Two are declined as nulls with reasons. The remaining five, and four halves of others, are drafted word for word at §7 below and enacted nowhere**, because each of them moves a loss between the survivor, the trust fund, the General Fund and the employing agency, and resolving that by drafting choice is the one thing this role may not do.

- **Store revision 58 is in the text**: [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), 506,848 characters, headroom 17,440, written on the live base `4e7afa69` and verified from the returned document JSON.
- **Eight substitutions, all inside new § 51.1-142.4**, in subdivisions G 4, D 1 and M 2. **+1,735 characters of bill text.** No figure moves, no designator is renumbered, no section joins or leaves the act, no defined term is added, and the title line does not change.
- Narrative §0.0-58; sweep §5.37; drafter's note §6.0-58; the nine drafted answers §7 item 122.

---

## 1. Every finding, and what happened to it

| # | Rank | Subject | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **F1** | **fatal** | The notwithstanding does not reach § 51.1-165.01 F; the certification then misstates it | **ENACTED (E1, E6).** The notwithstanding now names *"so much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163."* **C 2 is preserved rather than displaced** — see §6 item 2 — and the displacement alternative is drafted at §7(9). |
| **F2** | serious | *"As on"* is a comparative, not a deeming; *"in service"* is undefined in § 51.1-124.3 | **ENACTED (E1).** *"And for the purposes of § 51.1-162 the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply"* — § 51.1-165.01 F's own words, so the act borrows the Code's hook rather than inventing a deeming. |
| **F3** | serious | *"Computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision"* confines the base to the purchased months | **ENACTED (E1).** *"Computed **taking account of** the service credit credited under this subdivision."* This also disposes of the G 5 cancellation case without confining (f) — see §6 item 7 and §4(b). |
| **F4** | serious | Edit 3 grants review that edits 6 and 7 withhold; the B 4 e employer is excluded too | **ENACTED (E7, E8).** *"Or other person to whom this section requires a notice to be given"* in **both** of M 2's class lists. Cures F15's review side as well. |
| **F5** | serious | Subsection E's second limb is not carved out, so the credit may not produce the unreduced allowance it was priced on | **NOT ENACTED — drafted two ways at §7(1).** This is the ERF residual [MOO-97](/MOO/issues/MOO-97) was opened on. It costs money and the figure is the Fiscal & Impact Modeler's. |
| **F6** | serious | Three of the certification's four compelled propositions of law are inaccurate | **ENACTED (E6), all three.** C 1 named instead of all of subsection C, with C 2's saving stated; § 51.1-162 B's second condition added; § 51.1-162 C stated and *"in every other case"* replaced. |
| **F7** | serious | The certification duty has no consequence, and the remedy the issue assumed does not attach to it | **ENACTED (E6)** — and **the issue's premise was mine and it was wrong**; see §4(a). The consequence is procedural: a determination for subsection M, and a line in the subsection J report. The writing is also given the section's own name. |
| **F8** | serious | The 30-day notice period is unperformable as to a person identified later | **ENACTED (E3c)**, with F13(d) in the same clause. |
| **F9** | serious | The release restores a settled amount to the cap after the cash has left, and there is no path to reverse the release | **NOT ENACTED — (a) drafted three ways at §7(2), (b) drafted at §7(3).** Both move money. |
| **F10** | moderate | The release fires only on an *election*, so it misses the § 51.1-162 A case the act itself calls the general one | **NOT ENACTED — drafted at §7(4)**, together with F11's release half. Widening a release widens what the Commonwealth pays under subsection N. |
| **F11** | moderate | The definite singular *"the person entitled"* breaks the multi-survivor case | **HALF ENACTED (E3b).** *"Each person entitled"* in the addressee list. The release half is §7(4). |
| **F12** | moderate | The Board is compelled to state a period that does not exist; the 90 days is in § 51.1-162 **C** | **ENACTED (E3a)** as a conditional statement. Fixing a period in G 4 is drafted at §7(5). |
| **F13** | moderate | The crediting deadline has no reporter, no reviewer and no independent clock, and it defeats edit 4's hook | **(a) and (d) ENACTED (E2, E3c). (b) DECLINED as a null — it does not hold on the live body; see §4(c). (c) and (e) drafted at §7(6) and §7(7).** |
| **F14** | minor | The J hook departs from the section's own formula and carries a loose *"it"* | **ENACTED (E4).** |
| **F15** | moderate | M 2's new class depends on an appointment nobody is required to obtain | **Review side ENACTED (E7, E8). Payment side drafted at §7(8)**, because it names a payee. |
| **F16** | minor | (f)'s operative limb negates a mechanism that was never the operative cause | **ENACTED (E1).** *"§ 51.1-163 shall not apply to the member's death."* |
| §3 nit | — | *"In lieu of any other benefit"* drops § 51.1-162 B's limiting words | **ENACTED (E5).** *"In lieu of any other benefit **under that section**."* |

---

## 2. The eight substitutions, verbatim

Every FIND string was asserted to occur **exactly once in §1 and exactly once in the whole document** before anything was written, and every READ string was asserted absent. The kit that applied them derives every label from the live body and refuses to write on a failed assertion; it is at `moo97-store-revision-58-apply/` with `apply.py`, `edits.py` and `content.py`.

### E1 — subdivision G 4, the (f) sentence (F1, F2, F3, F16, and the C 2 conflict)

**FIND**

> Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board's receipt of a written notification of the member's effective date of retirement given under subdivision D 1 shall not cause § 51.1-163 to apply to the member's death, and the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision.

**READ**

> Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 <u>and so much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163</u>, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, <u>§ 51.1-163 shall not apply to the member's death and</u> the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service, computed <u>taking account of</u> the service credit credited under this subdivision<u>; and for the purposes of § 51.1-162 the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply. Nothing in the preceding sentence reduces a benefit payable under subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165, and where that subdivision applies the Board shall pay the benefit it provides or the benefit determined under the preceding sentence, whichever is greater.</u>

### E2 — subdivision G 4, the crediting deadline (F13(a))

**FIND** · The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death.

**READ** · The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death<u>, and shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to credit it within that period</u>.

### E3a — subdivision G 4, the death notice (F12)

**FIND** · under § 51.1-162 and of the period within which the waiver or election must be made

**READ** · under § 51.1-162 and<u>, where § 51.1-162 states a period within which the waiver or election must be made,</u> of <u>that</u> period

### E3b — subdivision G 4, the addressees (F11, notice half)

**FIND** · to the member's estate, to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, to any person who claimed

**READ** · to the member's estate, to <u>each</u> person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, to any person who claimed

### E3c — subdivision G 4, the notice period (F8 and F13(d))

**FIND** · no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit; a person to whom that notice is required to be given

**READ** · no later than 30 days after <u>the earlier of the date on which</u> it credits the service credit <u>and the last day on which this subdivision requires it to be credited or, as to a person whose entitlement or non-entitlement to any benefit payable on the member's death the Board determines after that date, no later than 30 days after that determination</u>; a person to whom that notice is required to be given

### E4 — subdivision G 4, the J hook (F14)

**FIND** · The Board shall state every failure to give the notice required by the preceding sentence within the period required by it in the report required by subsection J.

**READ** · The Board shall state <u>in the report required by subsection J</u> every failure to give the notice required by the preceding sentence within the period <u>this subdivision allows for it</u>.

### E5 — subdivision G 4, the release trigger (the §3 citation nit)

**FIND** · or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit, the Board shall release

**READ** · or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit <u>under that section</u>, the Board shall release

### E6 — subdivision D 1, the pre-filing certification (F6(a), (b), (c) and F7)

**FIND**

> The Board shall state in the writing required by this subdivision that, where a member whose election the Board has accepted dies after the Board has received the notification of the member's effective date of retirement required by this subdivision and before that date, the benefit payable on the member's death is determined under subdivision G 4 and under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service and not under subsection C of § 51.1-165; that no option elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 governs that benefit; that subsection B of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance on the death of a member in service only where the member is survived by a spouse, a minor child or a parent; and that in every other case subsection A of § 51.1-162 provides for the payment of the member's accumulated contributions.

**READ**

> <u>The Board's certification shall also state</u> that, where a member whose election the Board has accepted dies after the Board has received the notification of the member's effective date of retirement required by this subdivision and before that date, the benefit payable on the member's death is determined under subdivision G 4 and under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service and not under <u>subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 or under subsection F of § 51.1-165.01; that subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165, where it applies, entitles the person named as contingent annuitant to the benefit that subdivision provides or to the benefit so determined, whichever is greater; that no other</u> option elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 governs that benefit; that subsection B of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance on the death of a member in service only where the member is survived by a spouse, a minor child or a parent <u>and no benefit is payable under subsection C of that section; that subsection C of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance to a surviving spouse where the member's death results from a cause compensable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act (§ 65.2-100 et seq.); and that where no allowance is payable under subsection B or C of § 51.1-162,</u> subsection A of <u>that section</u> provides for the payment of the member's accumulated contributions. <u>A failure to state in the Board's certification every matter required by the preceding sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M, and the Board shall state every such failure in the report required by subsection J.</u>

### E7 and E8 — subsection M 2, both class lists (F4, F15 review side)

**FIND (E7)** · 2. A member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member's estate adversely affected by a determination

**READ (E7)** · 2. A member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, personal representative of a deceased member's estate<u>, or other person to whom this section requires a notice to be given,</u> adversely affected by a determination

**FIND (E8)** · limits the right of a member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member's estate aggrieved

**READ (E8)** · limits the right of a member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, personal representative of a deceased member's estate<u>, or other person to whom this section requires a notice to be given,</u> aggrieved

---

## 3. Corrections — three against the review, two against me, two against my own sweep

**(a) F7's premise was mine, and it fails on the words.** This issue's own work list reasoned that D 1's day-for-day extension carried the consequence of an incomplete certification because *"an incomplete statement is a late statement."* The extension sentence attaches to *"that written statement"* — the statement of earliest and final qualifying retirement dates required by the **definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A** — and the certification is a different writing. **The duty had no consequence at all**, not a weak one. The review is right and the premise is withdrawn.

**(b) F3's cancellation case needs no confinement of (f), and I did not take the fix direction for it.** The reviewer proposed adding *"and whose election has not been cancelled under subdivision 5."* With *"taking account of"* in place, the computation limb no longer points at a base that can be null: § 51.1-162's own computation runs on creditable service, and the credited months are taken account of in it, whether they were credited under G 4 or under G 5. **Confining (f) would have pushed the cancelling member back out to § 51.1-165 C 1 — a loss — to cure a defect that the smaller fix already closes.**

**(c) F13(b) does not hold on the live body, and the reason is store revision 55.** The review worked from store revision 54 (document revision `d453a9ee`). Subdivision M 2's second sentence — added as store revision 55's E5, out of [MOO-130](/MOO/issues/MOO-130)'s M1 — now provides that *"every determination, certification, redetermination, recertification, reduction, cancellation, rescission, restoration, **crediting of service credit**, placement on a waiting list, expiration of a reservation, denial of an election, and refusal to accept an election under this section is a determination of the Board for the purposes of this subsection."* M 2's first limb reaches *"a failure of the Board to make a determination … within a period required by this section."* **So a failure to credit within E2's 60 days is already reviewable and no words were written for it.** F13(a) and (d) are real and enacted; (b) is a null.

**(d) The reviewer's F1 fix direction named *"subsection F of § 51.1-165.01."* The enacted words name one limb of it.** Subsection F does two things, and only one of them is adverse: it routes the death to § 51.1-163, **and** it provides that *"the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply."* The second limb is the member's friend, and it is the authority F2's cure borrows. Displacing the whole subsection would have discarded the limb the act wants.

**(e) The reviewer's F1 fix direction also named subdivision C 2. C 2 is preserved instead.** See §6 item 2. The displacement alternative is §7(9) and is one substitution away.

**(f) Two counts in my own §5.37 were predictions and were wrong; the sweep is corrected in the document.** I published *"§ 51.1-165 bare 5 → 6"* and *"§ 51.1-162 6 → 11."* Re-counted mechanically over §1 of the written body: **bare § 51.1-165 is 5 → 7** and **§ 51.1-162 is 6 → 9**, because three of the new references say *"that section"* rather than repeating the citation and because the C 2 preservation sentence names § 51.1-165 twice. The corrected figures and a one-line note are in §5.37. **A predicted count is not a count** — the same lesson §5.33's failed assertion taught, in a smaller way.

**(g) §5.33's assertion that *"§ 51.1-165 is the only one whose operation the act alters"* was false when it was written**, and MOO-154's F1 is the finding that caught it. The stub §5.33 now carries the correction, and §5.37 states the rule it produces: **the citation count is not the cross-reference check; reading the cited section is.**

---

## 4. The two findings I declined, with reasons

1. **F13(b) — reviewability of a late crediting.** Declined as a null. See §3(c). Writing for it would have added a sentence that M 2 already performs, and a second route to the same remedy is a defect, not belt-and-braces.
2. **F3's confinement of (f) to uncancelled elections.** Declined. See §3(b). It would move a loss onto the cancelling member to fix something the enacted words already fix.

Neither declination is a judgment that the reviewer was careless: (b) turns on a sentence that landed in the store **after** the body the review read, and the review says which body it read.

---

## 5. The three provisions, reproduced in full as amended

Pulled verbatim from §1 of the written body of store revision 58, not retyped. New language is underlined in the bill because the whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language; the eight substitutions are therefore inside `<u>` runs and carry no separate markup. The redline for each is §2 above.

### Subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4, in full as amended

4. Subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply, and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, if the member, after the Board accepts the election, (i) dies, (ii) is approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or (iii) is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. For the purposes of clause (iii) of this subdivision, a member who retires at a time when the Board has not given a statement or notice of the member's final qualifying retirement date required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement or notice has expired, is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board; and a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given such a statement or notice and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. For the purposes of the preceding sentence, a statement or notice of the member's final qualifying retirement date required by that definition does not include the notice of the Board's determination upon a request, and of the reasons for it, that that definition requires to be given no later than 30 days after the request is filed, and the remedies of the member for a failure of the Board to give that notice are those provided by subdivision D 1, by that definition, and by subsection M. Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death. In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary. Notwithstanding the crediting required by the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2; shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death, and shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to credit it within that period. Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 and so much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, § 51.1-163 shall not apply to the member's death and the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service, computed taking account of the service credit credited under this subdivision; and for the purposes of § 51.1-162 the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply. Nothing in the preceding sentence reduces a benefit payable under subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165, and where that subdivision applies the Board shall pay the benefit it provides or the benefit determined under the preceding sentence, whichever is greater. Where the member dies, the Board shall give written notice of the service credit credited under this subdivision, of the benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary and of the computation of it, of any right of the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death to waive that benefit or to elect another benefit in its place under § 51.1-162 and, where § 51.1-162 states a period within which the waiver or election must be made, of that period, of the amount of any refund required by this subdivision, and of the reasons for the Board's determinations, to the member's estate, to each person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, to any person who claimed any benefit payable on the member's death and whom the Board determined is not entitled to it, and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf, no later than 30 days after the earlier of the date on which it credits the service credit and the last day on which this subdivision requires it to be credited or, as to a person whose entitlement or non-entitlement to any benefit payable on the member's death the Board determines after that date, no later than 30 days after that determination; a person to whom that notice is required to be given may seek review of any determination stated in it under subsection M; and the period within which such a person may seek review under subsection M of a determination stated in that notice runs from the date the notice is given to that person. The Board shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to give the notice required by the preceding sentence within the period this subdivision allows for it. Where the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit under that section, the Board shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2, no later than 60 days after the election, notwithstanding the requirement of subdivision D 2 that an amount settled remain charged against that limitation. Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision. Where the member is approved for a disability retirement allowance, the Board shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the commencement of a disability retirement allowance, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. The certified subsidy for an election to which clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of this subdivision applies and that is not settled under subdivision 1 is settled, and subsection N applies to that settlement as it applies to a settlement under subdivision 1, on the earliest of (a) the date of the member's death, (b) the effective date of a disability retirement allowance approved for the member, and (c) the effective date of a retirement that the member is unable to take as a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall make every recertification required by this subdivision before making the redetermination required by this subdivision, except that where a recertification becomes required after the redetermination has been made the Board shall make the recertification and shall thereupon redetermine the certified subsidy again as this subdivision requires. ## 7. Ambiguities resolved — nine, and none of them chose a policy

1. **F1's notwithstanding names a limb, not a subsection.** See §3(d). *"So much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163"* — twenty-one words that keep subsection F's disapplication of the in-service requirement alive and take away only its routing to a refund.
2. **Subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165 is preserved, not displaced — the judgment to attack first.** C 2 is a *saving* provision: it pays the **greater** of § 51.1-163 and § 51.1-162 B to a spouse, minor child or parent named under a joint and last-survivor option. Naming it in the notwithstanding, as the fix direction proposed, would take an existing right from a named class so that the act reads more simply. The enacted second sentence pays the greater of the two, so **no member is worse off than under present law**, and the conflict between an unrepealed saving provision and a later flat command is resolved on the face of the act. **The alternative is §7(9) below and is one substitution.**
3. **F13(b) is a null and the reason is a sentence that landed after the review.** See §3(c).
4. **F7's premise was mine and is withdrawn.** See §3(a). What replaces it is procedural and the section's own: a determination for subsection M, and a line in the subsection J report. **It is not a new remedy and it moves no money.**
5. **The certification is not given a new verb.** D 1's third sentence already reads *"The Board's certification shall state the matters required by…"*, so the enacted opener is *"The Board's certification shall also state"* — the same actor, the same formula, one clause shorter than the fix direction's *"The Board shall state in the Board's certification."* **Where the surrounding statute has a form, it beats the better sentence.**
6. **F6(c) is cured by stating § 51.1-162 C, not by deleting *"in every other case."*** A member about to file can act on the information, and it is the one case in which the purchased credit cannot change the benefit at all, because § 51.1-162 C measures on average final compensation and not on creditable service. **That consequence is a fiscal fact and it is routed, not drafted around.**
7. **F11 is cured in the addressee and nowhere else.** *"Each person entitled"* goes into the addressee list, because § 51.1-162 B divides an allowance among more than one minor child and among more than one parent, and a definite singular identifies no addressee where two persons are entitled. The **release** half, and F10's asymmetry with the no-election case, are one drafted answer at §7(4) — widening a release widens what the Commonwealth pays under subsection N.
8. **F8's and F13(d)'s cure is one clause, built as a floor and never a setter.** The notice period runs from *"the earlier of"* the date of crediting and the last day on which crediting was required, so **a Board that credits late cannot extend its own notice period**; and the alternative limb starts a fresh 30 days as to a person whose entitlement the Board determines later. Neither limb can pull a period forward against the Board; both can only bind it.
9. **F12 is cured by making the statement conditional, not by inventing a period.** § 51.1-162 **B** states none; the 90 days is in § 51.1-162 **C** and waives a C allowance to take a B allowance. Fixing a period would be a determination with no standard anywhere in the act. **It is drafted as an answer at §7(5) instead of taken.**

## 8. The nine drafted answers — word for word, and none of them enacted

**Four of these nine decide who bears a loss. I have not picked one.** Each is one substitution against the live text of store revision 58.

### (1) F5 — the unreduced-retirement-eligibility bar. The ERF residual, and the largest item here

The problem: subsection E's last sentence has two limbs, and G 4's saving (*"Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision"*) reaches only the **crediting** limb. The second limb — *"except for the purposes of the definition of 'eligible member' in subsection A, no member shall be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of an election before payment in full is received"* — stands unqualified in the death case. Clause (v) of *"eligible member"* means **every** member in G 4 is one whose unreduced eligibility depends on the purchase. So the survivor's § 51.1-162 B allowance may be computed **with** the § 51.1-155 A 2 or A 3 reduction, while *"certified subsidy"* priced the subsidy on *"the member's retirement on the member's anticipated earliest qualifying retirement date"* — unreduced retirement. **The Commonwealth pays for the unreduced outcome and the survivor is paid the reduced one.**

**Form A — every member whom the credited service carries over the line.** FIND *"Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision."* READ:

> Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision<u>, and does not prevent the member from being treated, for the purposes of § 51.1-162, as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date where the service credit credited under this subdivision causes him to have reached it</u>.

**Form B — only where payment was completed before death.** Same FIND. READ:

> Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision<u>, and, where the member completed payment for the whole of the service credit stated in the Board's certification before the date of death, does not prevent the member from being treated, for the purposes of § 51.1-162, as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date where that service credit causes him to have reached it</u>.

**A costs more than B. B leaves the partial payer reduced** — and the partial payer is the case G 4's own crediting sentence was written for. **The figure is the Fiscal & Impact Modeler's and neither form is priced.**

### (2) F9(a) — the $3,000,000 cap stops measuring Commonwealth money

Subsection N pays the settled amount to the retirement system **on settlement**, which G 4 fixes at the date of death; the release sentence then restores that amount to the cap, and nothing moves it back from the retirement system. Over the Program the Commonwealth's cash exposure becomes **the cap plus every released-and-already-paid amount, with no stated bound.**

**(i) Restore only what has not been paid.** READ: *"…shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available to be reserved under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2 <u>only to the extent the amount settled has not been paid to the retirement system under subsection N</u>, no later than 60 days after the election…"* **Keeps the cap a cash limit; gives the Program less capacity back than the current words promise.**

**(ii) Recover the cash.** Add: *"<u>and the retirement system shall repay to the appropriation from which it was paid so much of the amount settled as has been paid to it under subsection N, no later than 60 days after the release</u>."* **This takes money back out of the trust fund after settlement; [MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96)'s F-3 and Va. Const. art. X, § 11 both bear on it, and it should not be enacted without counsel on that point.**

**(iii) Leave it, and disclose it.** No edit. The cap then bounds *reservations* and not cash, and that must be stated in the fiscal note and in the memo's risk section. **This is a decision, not a default.**

### (3) F9(b) — a survivor who wins her review has nothing left to be paid out of

G 4 forbids a second settlement (*"no certified subsidy is settled more than once under this subdivision or under subdivision 1"*) and its reinstatement machinery is keyed to a released **reservation**, not to a released **amount settled**.

> <u>Where an amount released under the preceding sentence would not have been released had a determination of the Board been as it stands after reconsideration under subsection M or after judicial review, the Board shall reinstate the amount released, together with any contingency amount released with it, no later than 30 days after the determination is reconsidered or reviewed, and the rule of this subdivision that no certified subsidy is settled more than once does not prevent the settlement of an amount so reinstated.</u>

**It restores a right and it costs what the right costs.**

### (4) F10 and F11's release half — the election case and the no-election case

Under § 51.1-162 **A** there is no election; A operates automatically where the relation test fails. So the unmarried member with no minor child and no surviving parent — identical economics, no allowance ever payable — frees nothing from the cap, while the electing survivor's case does.

**FIND** *"Where the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit under that section,"* **READ**:

> <u>Where no retirement allowance is payable under § 51.1-162 on the member's death, whether because the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit under that section or because no such allowance is payable to any person,</u>

**It also cures the two-minor-children case**, where one guardian elects and an allowance is still payable to the other child: the release no longer fires while an allowance remains payable. **It widens what the cap gives back, so it interacts with (2) and should be decided with it.**

### (5) F12's alternative — state a period in G 4 for the § 51.1-162 B election

> <u>A waiver or election under § 51.1-162 in respect of a death to which this subdivision applies shall be made no later than 90 days after the Board gives the notice required by this subdivision, and the Board shall act upon it no later than 30 days after it is made.</u>

**It closes (2)(iii)'s open-ended driver and it takes a right from a survivor who is slow.** Ninety days is § 51.1-162 C's own figure, which is why it is the one proposed; the numeral would be mine and that is why it is here.

### (6) F13(c) — nothing requires anyone to tell the Board the member died

> <u>A state agency that employs or last employed a member whose election the Board has accepted shall give the Board written notice of the member's death no later than 30 days after the agency learns of it, and the Board shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure of a state agency to give that notice of which the Board becomes aware.</u>

Drafted on the model of G 4's own involuntary-separation limb, which pairs *"learns of"* with exactly this duty and this report. **It is a new duty on employing agencies. It is confined to state agencies, because a duty on a local employer needs an express grant and a Dillon's Rule judgment that is not mine to make.**

### (7) F13(e) — a deadline that can expire before the Board can begin

The redetermination runs *"no later than 90 days after that date"* — the date of death. Where the Board learns of the death later than that, it is already late, and G 4's escape sentence covers a recertification that *"becomes required after the redetermination has been made,"* not a deadline that expired before the Board knew.

**FIND** *"The Board shall, no later than 90 days after that date, redetermine"* **READ**:

> The Board shall, no later than 90 days after that date <u>or, where that date is the date of the member's death, no later than 90 days after the date on which the Board learns of the death</u>, redetermine

**It is a timing change to a period you set, and it only ever moves the deadline later.**

### (8) F15's payment side — a refund payable to an estate that may never exist

G 4 directs the refund and the notice to *"the member's estate"*, and nothing in the act, in Chapter 1 or in Title 64.2 requires a personal representative to qualify.

> <u>Where no personal representative of the member's estate has qualified, the Board shall pay the amount payable to the estate under this subdivision, and shall give the notice required by this subdivision, to the person who received the member's accumulated contributions under § 51.1-162 or, where no person has received them, to the person who would be entitled to receive them under subsection A of that section.</u>

**It names a payee, which is why it is yours and not mine.** It also makes that person a notice addressee, and therefore — by E7 and E8 — a person who may seek review under subsection M.

### (9) F1's alternative — displace subdivision C 2 instead of preserving it

**READ for E1's opening**, in place of what is enacted: *"Notwithstanding subdivision<u>s</u> C 1 <u>and C 2</u> of § 51.1-165 and so much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163, …"*, with the second sentence (*"Nothing in the preceding sentence reduces a benefit payable under subdivision C 2…"*) **deleted**, and the certification's C 2 limb deleted with it.

**Simpler by about 230 characters, and it takes an existing right** from a spouse, minor child or parent named under a joint and last-survivor option whose refund of contributions would have been the greater of the two. **One substitution either way.**

### Still open and not re-asked here

**§7 item 60's (a), (b) and (c)** — the elected-option class whose contingent annuitant is a sibling, an adult child or an unmarried partner. (f) routes her death to § 51.1-162, and § 51.1-162 B pays only a spouse, minor child or parent, so **she is still unanswered**, and MOO-154 does not change that. **Item 106's three alternatives for the certification's wording are superseded by E6** and should be read against the words now enacted. **Item 107** is store revision 55's and is untouched.

## 10. Three sentences for the Editor

**This revision fixes a hole that would have made the bill's death-benefit promise false for most of the state employees who rely on it: the text displaced one provision that sends a pre-retirement death to a refund of the member's own contributions, but not the twin provision that does the same thing for anyone who takes a partial lump sum, which is the ordinary way a Virginia state employee retires. It also stops the Board being required to tell a member four things about her own death benefit, three of which were not the law, and it gives two people the act hands a notice — a rejected claimant and an employer that paid part of the member's cost — the right to ask the Board to think again. What it does not yet do is guarantee that the service credit the Commonwealth paid to accelerate actually produces the unreduced allowance it was priced on; that question, and three about who bears a loss, are in front of the Policy Director.**

## 1. §7 item 36 — the partial-lump-sum tier notice. Drafted in full; **recommended, not agreed, and not in the bill.**

### 1.1 The gap, with the clause letters now settled

A member admitted to this pilot stands at the unreduced-retirement door **by construction**: clause
(vi) of *"eligible member"* admits only a member who would reach her unreduced retirement eligibility
date on or before the first day of the month following her application, and clause (viii) requires the
same of the credit as actually purchased. § 51.1-165.01 B measures its 12-, 24- and 36-month
partial-lump-sum tiers in *"service performed after"* the date the member was first eligible for an
unreduced service retirement allowance. So:

- the **1x tier** (12 months of post-eligibility service) is reachable on **exactly one date** — the
  member's final qualifying retirement date — because the earliest date the tier is satisfied and the
  latest date subsection F permits are the same single date, and
- the **2x and 3x tiers are not reachable at all** by a member who retires in a qualifying retirement.

Nothing in the bill tells her. The full working, including the arithmetic and the three corrections to
the item as it was routed, is [`moo92-record`](/MOO/issues/MOO-92#document-moo92-record) §§1.1 to 1.3,
which stays the system of record for the reasoning. Two things in that record have since changed:
MOO-87's clause letters are settled (above), and the margin M 2's tolling gave the 1x tier is now
**capped at 120 days** by revision 24, which tightens the item rather than relieving it.

### 1.2 The candidate text — two sentences, and I recommend both or neither

Both go in the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* in subsection A. **Nothing else in
the bill is touched.** The first sentence is inserted immediately after *"…no later than 15 days after
the approval."*; the second immediately after the sentence that begins *"A written statement or notice
is given for the purposes of this section…"*, which is where it has to sit if it is to qualify that
sentence rather than contradict it.

**Sentence 1 — the notice.**

> **The Board shall state in the written statement required by this definition (i) that the member's
> retirement does not fail to be a qualifying retirement, and that the service credit purchased under
> the member's election does not fail to vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of
> § 51.1-142.2, by reason of the member's election of an option under § 51.1-165 or of a partial
> lump-sum option under § 51.1-165.01, and (ii) the effect of subsection B of § 51.1-165.01 upon the
> member, including that a member who remains in service beyond the member's final qualifying
> retirement date does not retire in a qualifying retirement and is subject to subsection G.**

**Sentence 2 — the consequence.**

> **A written statement that omits a statement required by this definition is not given for the
> purposes of this section until the Board gives the member the omitted statement.**

**Why sentence 2 is not optional.** Sentence 1 names the actor (the Board), the object (the two
statements) and the deadline (it rides the existing 15-day deadline in the same sentence group). On its
own it has **no consequence for an incomplete statement**, and a statement given on time but missing
limb (ii) is exactly the failure the provision exists to prevent. Sentence 2 makes an incomplete
statement a late statement, and subdivision D 1 already carries the consequence: *"Where the Board
gives that written statement … later than the time required by that definition, the member's final
qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of days by which the statement or notice is
late."* No new remedy is invented and no new period is created. **A notice duty with no consequence is
the defect my own output bar tells me not to file**, so I recommend enacting both sentences or neither.

### 1.3 The definition in full as it would read if item 36 is enacted

Reproduced entire, so the rule is readable without this note. **Bold** is what the two candidate
sentences add; nothing is removed.

> "Final qualifying retirement date" means the date that is 12 months after the member's earliest qualifying retirement date, except that the Board shall approve a later date where the Board's own processing requirements, or any other cause not attributable to the member, make the member's retirement on or before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition impracticable. A later date approved under this definition shall be the first day of a month and shall be not more than three months after the date determined under the first sentence of this definition. The Board shall approve a later date on its own initiative or upon the written request of the member, which the member may file at any time before the date that would otherwise apply under this definition or before any later date approved under this definition; the Board shall act upon such a request, and shall give the member written notice of its determination and of the reasons for it, no later than 30 days after the request is filed; and the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M. The Board shall determine the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date, and shall state both of them and the reasons for any later date approved under this definition, in writing to the member no later than 15 days after the Board credits to the member the service credit purchased under the member's election, and shall give the member written notice of any later date approved after that statement no later than 15 days after the approval. **The Board shall state in the written statement required by this definition (i) that the member's retirement does not fail to be a qualifying retirement, and that the service credit purchased under the member's election does not fail to vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, by reason of the member's election of an option under § 51.1-165 or of a partial lump-sum option under § 51.1-165.01, and (ii) the effect of subsection B of § 51.1-165.01 upon the member, including that a member who remains in service beyond the member's final qualifying retirement date does not retire in a qualifying retirement and is subject to subsection G.** A written statement or notice is given for the purposes of this section on the date the Board mails it to the member or transmits it to the member electronically, except that where the Board mails it, every period that runs from the giving of the statement or notice is extended by three days. **A written statement that omits a statement required by this definition is not given for the purposes of this section until the Board gives the member the omitted statement.** Where the member's final qualifying retirement date as extended under this definition, as extended under subdivision D 1, or as tolled under subsection M is not the first day of a month, the member's final qualifying retirement date is the first day of the next month.


### 1.4 The three choices inside item 36, stated as choices

1. **Limb (i) is narrower than the routing issue asked for, deliberately.** The ask was notice that the
   election *"does not affect her settlement under subdivision G 1."* That is wider than the text
   supports. What the MOO-65 F-1 proviso settles is that her retirement does not stop being a
   *qualifying retirement* and her credit still vests at the pilot cost, because both *"qualifying
   retirement"* and *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* are determined *"as though no option had
   been elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 and no lump-sum distribution had been paid under
   § 51.1-165.01."* It does **not** settle the *quantum* of the G 1 redetermination: the definition of
   *"certified subsidy"* carries no such proviso and values *"the benefits payable under this chapter
   to the member and to the member's survivors and beneficiaries,"* and a partial lump-sum changes the
   form in which those benefits are paid. **Nothing lands on the member either way** — G 1 says a
   redetermination *"shall not create any obligation of the member"* and the amount settled is capped
   at *"the amount last certified and reserved"* — so the residue is a trust-fund question for
   [@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50) and not a member-facing
   one. A notice saying the election *"does not affect her settlement"* would tell her something the
   text does not say.
2. **Limb (ii) describes the effect of § 51.1-165.01 B rather than declaring its meaning.** The obvious
   draft would have the bill state what § 51.1-165.01 B means. I rejected it: a construction of a
   section this act does not amend, placed in the Code, invites the argument that the act amended
   § 51.1-165.01 by implication and changed the rule for every other purchased-service member in the
   system; and if the Board's construction moves, the bill is left asserting a rule the administering
   agency no longer applies. The Board administers § 51.1-165.01. The bill reserves to itself only the
   proposition it controls — that staying on past the final qualifying retirement date forfeits the
   qualifying retirement and drops the member into subsection G.
3. **Sentence 2 says "for the purposes of this section," not "of this definition."** The sentence it
   qualifies — *"A written statement or notice is given for the purposes of this section on the date
   the Board mails it…"* — uses the section-wide formulation, and D 1's day-for-day extension is a
   section-wide consequence. Matching the scope is what makes the two sentences one rule instead of two
   competing ones. Note the deliberate reach: *"a statement required by this definition"* catches an
   omission of the **two dates and the reasons for a later approved date** as well as the two new
   limbs, because an omitted date is the same failure as an omitted warning.

**Where it goes, and the alternative rejected.** The Stakeholder Analyst offered subdivision D 1 as the
other home. D 1 is where the § 51.1-153 notice periods live and it is already the longest subdivision
in the section; the *"final qualifying retirement date"* definition is where the Board's statement of
the two dates is created, and this notice is about those two dates. It belongs with the dates.

**The three things notice does not do, and all three are policy.** Notice tells her about the
collision; it does not remove it. Lengthening the window re-opens the priced quantity and the dial
MOO-48's ladder is built on. Disapplying § 51.1-165.01 B's post-eligibility clock for pilot members
adds a **third amended section** to an act that amends one and adds one, is an unpriced benefit
enhancement, and changes a rule reaching far beyond the pilot — against the minimal-footprint rule, and
**I do not recommend it.** The third route is to leave the tiers unreachable and say so, which is what
item 36 does, and it is my recommendation: the pilot's bargain is a cheap purchase in exchange for
retiring inside a 12-month window, and a member who wants three years of post-eligibility work does not
want this bargain. Telling her before she pays is the whole of what she is owed.
`moo92-record` §1.5 carries the same three routes at length.

| § 51.1-165 | Yes | Already cited in the definitions of *"qualifying retirement"* and *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*. The candidate adds no new citation form and no new section to the act. |

D 1 refers to it by a longer form — *"the written statement of the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date first required by the definition of 'final qualifying retirement date' in subsection A"* — and it is the same instrument. No ambiguity created. |
| Clauses (v), (vi) and (viii) of *"eligible member"* | Yes | The door-at-the-threshold construction the item rests on. Lettering is MOO-87's as landed in store revision 29: the new clause (vii) is the one-month-advance bar and the old clause (vii) is now **(viii)**. The candidate text cites none of them; §7 item 36 does. |

**Conforming amendments required elsewhere in the Code: none.** The candidate adds a notice duty inside
a new section and construes no other section. **One consequential check inside the bill:** subdivision
M 2 tolls *"any period within which the member must act under this section."* Both candidate sentences
impose periods on the **Board**, not on the member, so M 2 does not reach them and no interaction
arises. **Enactment clauses: nothing to add** — both sentences sit inside § 51.1-142.4 and expire with
it under enactment 3, leaving no stranded reference.

## 2. §7 item 37 — G 4's death-deeming against the A 2 / A 3 reduction. **Enacted in store revision 31**, and it is neither candidate (a) nor candidate (b).

### 2.1 What [MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96) answered

**The reading is narrow.** The A 2 / A 3 early-retirement reduction survives the deeming, so the bill
as drafted already produces the narrow result on the better reading. Counsel's reason is one the
routing record did not reach: limb (ii) of the definition of *"qualifying retirement"* is a **route
filter** lifted near-verbatim from § 51.1-153 B 2 and B 3's own phrasing, in the indicative, describing
an **outcome** of applying § 51.1-155 rather than switching it off — and because § 51.1-155 A 2 and A 3
themselves produce no reduction at 30 or more years of service, *"is not reduced under subdivision A 2
or A 3"* presupposes that § 51.1-155 **is** applied. The *expressio unius* argument that produced the
wide reading, run to completion, also strips the *"as though no option had been elected under
§ 51.1-165"* limb, which collides head-on with § 51.1-162 B's measure — *"the **decreased** retirement
allowance that would have been payable under the joint and survivor option"* — so the canon proves too
much. Full reading: [`red-team-reading`](/MOO/issues/MOO-96#document-red-team-reading).

**Three consequences for this drafting, and the third is the one that mattered.**

1. The wide reading is **not** the one the words bear, so **this is not a pricing item** on the ground
   the work list anticipated. (Two pricing items survive on other grounds — §5 below.)
2. **Leaving the text alone is still indefensible.** The ambiguity is real and a survivor's counsel has
   a live argument on maximally sympathetic facts. Candidate **(c)** is out.
3. **Candidate (a) is worse than the defect.** Counsel rates it **fatal to (a)** as drafted: it adds a
   *second* enumerated disapplication list to a sentence that already has one, and again omits the
   no-option limb, so the residual claim it leaves (**$195,034 PV per case**) is larger than the one it
   closes (**$146,729**). Candidate (b) is the wide reading made express and the reading is not wide.

**So the enacted text is a third clause, written to counsel's direction:** disapply the definition **as
a whole** for the death calculation rather than enumerating limbs, say nothing affirmative about which
section computes, fix the § 51.1-153 limb, and use one formulation for the payee.

### 2.2 The five findings the enacted text answers, and how

| Finding | What was wrong | What the enacted text does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **F-1** (fatal to candidate (a)) | Any enumeration of the definition's limbs strengthens the inference that the un-enumerated *"as though no option had been elected under § 51.1-165"* limb survives into the death calculation. | **No enumeration.** One clause: *"and that definition does not govern the calculation of any such benefit."* The definition is disapplied **as a whole** for the calculation, so there is no list to run the canon against. |
| **F-4** (serious) | § 51.1-165 C routes a **filed-notice** death to § 51.1-163 and deems retirement on the **effective date**, not the date of death. G 4 never mentioned it, and candidate (a)'s *"as § 51.1-162 requires"* would have overridden it. This is the modal end-of-window member. | **No section is named.** The payment limb now reads *"as this chapter otherwise provides,"* and the deeming is confined *"for the purposes of this section."* The chapter's own routing — including § 51.1-165 C — therefore governs both which provision computes and on what date, and the date conflict dissolves because G 4 no longer purports to fix a date for the survivor benefit. |
| **F-7** (moderate) | The deeming disapplied three **date** requirements but not the § 51.1-153 limb, whose own requirements — written notification of an effective date, and an effective date after the member's last day of service — are equally impossible for a dead member. **Unfixed by both (a) and (b).** The risk ran **against** the member: the Board declines to credit the purchased service at the pilot cost because no § 51.1-153 service retirement can be deemed, and bills the estate standard cost. | New clause: *"and no other requirement of that definition, and no requirement of § 51.1-153, that a deceased member cannot satisfy applies to the retirement so deemed."* |
| **F-8** (moderate) | Two formulations for one quantity — *"any benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary."* Under § 51.1-162 A the fourth person in the order of precedence is *"the duly appointed executor or administrator of the estate,"* arguably neither a survivor nor a beneficiary. | One formulation, used once and then referred back to: *"the member's survivor, beneficiary, or estate"*, and then *"any such benefit."* |
| **§6 of the reading** — "say what the deemed retirement is deemed **for**" | The sentence deemed at large and a reader had to infer the purposes. Counsel also advised **against deleting** *"in a qualifying retirement"*: strip it and the Board gains an argument that the pilot-cost conditions were never met, which runs against the estate. | The phrase **stays** and is confined by scope rather than by enumeration: *"for the purposes of this section."* Every consumer of a qualifying retirement that must operate on death is inside the section — the crediting and vesting limb of G 4 itself, subsection F, the subdivision D 6 recertification, the settlement limb of G 4, subsection D 7's non-release rule, and subsection N. **I verified that § 51.1-142.2 as amended uses the term nowhere**, so *"this section"* strands nothing. |

### 2.3 The redline

**Struck:**

> …and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor ~~or beneficiary as though the member had~~ retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death, and for that purpose the requirements of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the effective date of retirement be the first day of a month and fall no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply.

**As enacted:**

> …and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor**, beneficiary, or estate as this chapter otherwise provides; the member is deemed, for the purposes of this section, to have** retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death, and for that purpose the requirements of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the effective date of retirement be the first day of a month and fall no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply**, and no other requirement of that definition, and no requirement of § 51.1-153, that a deceased member cannot satisfy applies to the retirement so deemed; and that definition does not govern the calculation of any such benefit**.

**Net: 311 characters, 68 words added and six removed. One sentence, not four** — and that is a
drafting constraint rather than a style preference. The next sentence of G 4 begins *"Notwithstanding
the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment…"*, and *"the preceding
sentence"* must keep pointing at the crediting instruction. Splitting the repair into separate sentences
would have re-pointed it at the last thing added. The three limbs are therefore separated by
semicolons inside the existing sentence, and the three express date disapplications are **kept**, on
counsel's finding that they are necessary and correctly chosen and that the new general clause does not
reliably subsume them: whether a particular date of death falls on the first of a month is a fact about
the date, not a requirement a deceased member *cannot satisfy*.

### 2.4 Subdivision G 4 in full as amended

Reproduced entire, so the rule is readable without this note. **Bold** is what store revision 31 adds,
~~struck~~ what it removes; everything else is store revision 30's text unchanged.

> 4. Subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply, and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, if the member, after the Board accepts the election, (i) dies, (ii) is approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or (iii) is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death. In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor ~~or beneficiary as though the member had~~**, beneficiary, or estate as this chapter otherwise provides; the member is deemed, for the purposes of this section, to have** retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death, and for that purpose the requirements of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the effective date of retirement be the first day of a month and fall no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply**, and no other requirement of that definition, and no requirement of § 51.1-153, that a deceased member cannot satisfy applies to the retirement so deemed; and that definition does not govern the calculation of any such benefit**. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2; shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost, and shall give written notice of the service credit credited, of the amount refunded, and of the reasons for the determination to the member's estate and to any such employer no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit. Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision. Where the member is approved for a disability retirement allowance, the Board shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the commencement of a disability retirement allowance, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. The certified subsidy for an election to which clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of this subdivision applies and that is not settled under subdivision 1 is settled, and subsection N applies to that settlement as it applies to a settlement under subdivision 1, on the earliest of (a) the date of the member's death, (b) the effective date of a disability retirement allowance approved for the member, and (c) the effective date of a retirement that the member is unable to take as a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall make every recertification required by this subdivision before making the redetermination required by the following sentence. The Board shall, no later than 90 days after that date, redetermine the certified subsidy in the manner provided in subdivision 1 but substituting that date for the member's actual effective date of retirement, the amount settled shall be the amount so redetermined or the amount last certified and reserved for the election, whichever is less, and the Board shall release the amount by which the amount reserved for the election, together with the contingency amount reserved under subdivision D 3, exceeds the amount settled. No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect. Where a reservation has been released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, the Board shall reinstate it, and the reinstated reservation shall be charged against the limitations in subdivision D 2 notwithstanding that the amount available to be reserved is thereby exceeded. A redetermination under this subdivision shall not create any obligation of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of any employer, shall not reduce the service credit credited to the member, and shall not affect any allowance or benefit payable to the member or to any survivor or beneficiary of the member. A transfer of the member's employment from one state agency to another state agency shall not affect an election. If the member incurs an involuntary separation after the Board accepts the election, subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2 if the member retires in a qualifying retirement no later than 90 days after the date of the involuntary separation. A member who retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement has not so retired for the purposes of this subdivision. If the member does not so retire, subdivision 2 shall apply, and the Board shall make the determination required by subdivision 2 within 60 days after the earliest of the expiration of that 90-day period, the member's final qualifying retirement date, if any, and the date on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement. The Board shall give the member written notice, no later than 15 days after the Board learns of the involuntary separation, of the date by which the member must retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and of the consequences under subdivision 2 of not retiring by that date. No amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or estate of a member on account of an involuntary separation or of any other event to which this subdivision applies, and nothing in this subdivision creates any liability of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of the member's estate to the retirement system, to an employer, or to the Commonwealth.

### 2.6 What item 37 does **not** reach — and these are not drafting

Counsel's four remaining serious findings are not curable by any amendment to G 4's deeming sentence,
and I have not attempted one. They are routed in §5.

- **F-2 — the vesting line.** The monthly survivor benefit requires five years of **creditable
  service**, and the pilot **adds** creditable service. A member with 4 years 2 months who purchases
  2 years and dies in service converts her spouse's refund into a lifetime annuity. The word *"vest"*
  appears nowhere in § 51.1-162; the gate is § 51.1-153's five-year condition read through
  § 51.1-162 B's counterfactual, which is exactly why it moves when creditable service moves. **This is
  the "shall credit the service credit purchased" limb, not the deeming.** It needs a conscious
  decision — price it, or add a vesting-at-death condition — and a number, and neither exists.
- **F-3 — the funding clause and the impact statement.** Any uplift lands **entirely in the trust
  fund**, because the Commonwealth's payment is capped at *"the amount last certified and reserved"* and
  a redetermination *"shall not affect any allowance or benefit payable."* Va. Const. art. X, § 11
  requires that *"[r]etirement system benefits shall be funded using methods which are consistent with
  generally accepted actuarial principles,"* and Va. Code § 30-19.1:7 requires a VRS impact statement.
  The construction has to be settled before introduction so the statement prices the design the bill
  actually enacts.
- **F-5 — the subsection C death.** § 51.1-162 C — a death compensable under the Workers' Compensation
  Act — pays a percentage of **average final compensation with no creditable-service term at all**, and
  it **displaces** subsection B entirely. So the purchased credit changes that survivor's allowance by
  **$0** while the certified subsidy still settles on the date of death under G 4's settlement sentence.
  That cohort bears the purchase price for zero benefit and appears nowhere in the stakeholder map.
- **The fiscal shape, recorded so nobody re-derives it as a worst case.** Counsel priced the exposure on
  the model's own basis: expected **$4,946 to $16,319 PV against D0's $1,641,824** trust cost — **0.3%
  to 1.0%**. *"This is not a fiscal problem. It is an equity, precedent and litigation problem."* The
  number to carry is the **per-event** one: **$70,000 to $250,490 PV** for a single survivor's claim.
  I assert none of these figures as mine; they are counsel's, with their basis stated in
  [`red-team-reading`](/MOO/issues/MOO-96#document-red-team-reading) §8.

## 3. §7 item 38 — M 2's tolling. **Cured in store revision 24; the numeral is mine.**

`moo92-record` §1.3(b) found that subdivision M 2 tolled the final qualifying retirement date on the
**filing** of a request under the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* and not on its
success, that the definition permitted a further filing *"before any later date approved under this
definition,"* and that the three-month cap in that definition limits an **approved** extension and not
the tolling. It did not draft a cure, because capping a tolling provision changes the pilot's calendar
and §7 item 25 records that the calendar is the Director's.

**Store revision 24 had already cured it, independently, as pass 7's F-1.** M 2 now reads, in relevant
part, that the filing *"tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date … until 30
days after the Board acts upon the request, **except that (i) no second or subsequent request for
reconsideration of the same determination, and no second or subsequent request under that definition,
tolls any period** under this section or under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, and **(ii) the
aggregate of all tolling under this subsection shall not exceed 120 days**."* The companion repair
anchored the three-month cap to *"the date determined under the first sentence of this definition"* so
that repetition cannot stack. §6.0-24 records the corrected statement of the window — **12 months, plus
the three-month processing extension, plus at most 120 days of tolling, plus any days of the Board's own
lateness** — and withdraws §6.0-18 item 8.

**So nothing is drafted here, and one thing is owed to you.** Both limbs are mine: the **120 days** and
the choice to exclude second and subsequent requests rather than to cap them. `moo92-record`'s candidate
was **90 days**. 120 is defensible on the face of the section — it is 30 days for the Board to act plus
30 days of post-decision tolling, twice over — but it is not a numeral any cited document directs, and
the standing principle in §7 is that my own chosen numbers are recorded rather than assumed.
**§7 item 38 asks you to confirm or move it, and nothing else.** One interaction worth knowing: this
tolling is the only margin the 1x partial-lump-sum tier has (`moo92-record` §1.3(b)), so **cutting it
tightens item 36** and the two items should be answered together.

## 4. Drafter's note — every ambiguity resolved in this revision, and how

1. **I enacted item 37 into the bill and left items 36 and 38 in §7.** The line I drew: item 37 is a
   **defect cure in words that are mine**, directed by a cited document ([MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96)),
   and it preserves the Director's decided treatment of G 4 rather than changing it — the narrow
   reading *is* the middle treatment decided on 12 October 2026. Item 36 is a provision **no cited
   document directs**: it is recommended, not agreed. Item 38 is a numeral. The standing rule in this
   file is that a provision no cited document directs goes to §7 and not into the text, and revision 24
   and revision 30 both enacted counsel-directed defect cures the same way.
2. **I drafted a third candidate rather than choosing between (a) and (b).** Counsel rated (a) fatal as
   drafted and (b) is the wide reading made express. Choosing either would have been choosing a policy
   that was never agreed. The third clause implements the reading counsel reached and changes no
   policy — which is why it is enacted rather than offered.
3. **"For the purposes of this section," not an enumerated list of purposes.** Counsel's §6 suggested
   naming the purposes — crediting, subsection F, subdivision D 6, subsection N. I rejected the
   enumeration for the same reason F-1 condemns candidate (a): an express list invites the inference
   that an omitted consumer is excluded, and the consumers of a qualifying retirement are spread across
   six provisions and may yet grow. A scope limit does the same work without a list, and I verified by
   search that the term appears nowhere outside the section.
4. **I kept the three express date disapplications.** The new general clause reaches a requirement *"that
   a deceased member cannot satisfy."* Whether a given date of death is the first of a month is a fact
   about the date, not an incapacity of a deceased member, so the general clause does **not** reliably
   subsume the three. Counsel's §10 independently found all three *"necessary and correctly chosen."*
5. **I dropped the affirmative "shall pay … as though" construction and did not replace it with a named
   section.** Counsel's (a)-2 and (a)-3: an affirmative command to compute under one section is
   surplusage whose only available work is displacement, and the section it would displace is the
   § 51.1-165 C routing that governs the modal end-of-window member. *"As this chapter otherwise
   provides"* keeps the actor and the duty and leaves the routing where the chapter put it. **Named
   actor, object and consequence are present; the deadline is the chapter's own**, which is a choice
   and I am recording it as one — a reader looking for *when* the Board must pay is sent to
   § 51.1-162 and § 51.1-163, not to this section.
6. **One sentence with semicolons rather than four sentences**, because the next sentence of G 4 says
   *"Notwithstanding the preceding sentence"* and re-pointing it would have been a silent defect in a
   provision nobody asked me to touch. §2.3.
7. **I did not delete *"in a qualifying retirement."*** Counsel's item-4 answer: deleting it gives the
   Board an argument that the pilot-cost conditions were never met, which runs **against** the estate in
   a case where the member is dead. The phrase stays and is confined.
8. **Item 36's limb (i) is narrower than the ask, and limb (ii) describes rather than declares.** §1.4
   items 1 and 2, carried from `moo92-record` §1.4 unchanged.
9. **Item 36's sentence 2 uses "for the purposes of this section"** to match the sentence it qualifies
   and the D 1 consequence it borrows, and it reaches an omission of the two dates as well as of the two
   new limbs. §1.4 item 3.
10. **I did not draft a cure for M 2's tolling, and I did not re-open the 120-day numeral.** It is
    enacted, it is defensible, and moving it is the Director's. §3.
11. **I corrected the work list rather than executing it.** Three of its items were already closed and
    its item numerals were stale. Executing the promotion instruction it warned about would have
    reverted four repairs; executing its renumbering would have renumbered an item twice. §0.
12. **I moved §0's revision-20 narrative out of the store document to buy headroom**, verbatim and with
    every lettered subsection label preserved, by the method store revisions 23, 24 and 30 used. Nothing
    was rewritten and nothing was summarised away. It is housekeeping and it is recorded because it
    changes where a `§0.000000000000000`-style reference resolves.

**For the Editor, in three sentences.** Store revision 31 makes one change to the bill: when a pilot
member dies before retiring, the Board credits the service credit she paid for and the survivor's
benefit is then computed under the ordinary death-benefit rules of the chapter, not under the pilot's
own definition of a qualifying retirement. That closes an argument that the survivor was entitled to an
**unreduced** allowance the member never earned — worth up to a quarter of a million dollars per case
and payable entirely out of the trust fund — without changing what anyone is owed on the intended
reading. Two items for the Director remain open on this revision: whether to warn members that electing
a partial lump sum cannot reach the higher tiers, and whether 120 days is the right cap on tolling.
