# Store revision 45 — the full record: §7 item 60 answered, the death branch's measure named, and one notice duty for every death

**MOO-97 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

This is the record proper for store revision 45 of
[`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), on the convention store revisions 33, 36,

## 1. The redline

**Three changes, all inside subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4. No figure moves, no definition is
added, no section joins the act, no designator is renumbered, and the title of the bill does not
change.**

**Change 1 — deleted, 972 characters down to 147.** The words struck below come out:

> In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit
> payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary ~~as though the member had retired in a qualifying
> retirement on the date of death, and for that purpose the requirements of the definition of
> "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the effective date of retirement be the first day of a
> month and fall no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the
> member's final qualifying retirement date shall not apply, no requirement of § 51.1-153 or of
> subdivision D 1 as to the member being in service, as to written notification by the member to the

   death sentence, but two later sentences of G 4 anchor on *"the preceding sentence"* — the
   partial-payment sentence and the refund sentence — so a sentence inserted after the death sentence
   would have re-pointed both. It is enacted **at the end of the death branch**, immediately before
   *"Subsection E does not prevent …"*, which is where item 60 (d) proposed it and which leaves every
   anchor reading what it read before. **The measure is general to the subdivision**, so position does
   not narrow it.
2. **Nothing of the disapplications survives, and that is the point of taking (d).** Store revision 40
   spent 423 characters enumerating what a dead member cannot satisfy; store revision 37 spent 143 before
   it. All of it is gone, because a requirement only had to be switched off while the text **deemed** a
   retirement that could not have happened. The chapter's in-service death benefit asks no question a
   deceased member must answer. **I am recording the reversal of my own two revisions explicitly** so
   that nobody later restores half of it on the strength of §6.0-40.
3. **A scope defect in the old notice limb, found here rather than by the review, and cured.** *"and
   shall give written notice …"* sat inside the *"except that … adverse federal tax consequence"*
   clause, whose nearest subject is that clause's own *"the Board shall apply"*. On the strict reading
   the partial payer was owed notice **only** where her refund could not be paid for tax reasons. Lifting
   the notice into its own sentence answers F8 and cures that at the same time, and it is why the change
   is a re-cut rather than an addition.
4. **The notice's contents and its three addressees.** It carries everything the struck limb carried —
   the service credit, any refund, the Board's reasons — and adds **the benefit and its computation**,
   which is the only element that makes (d) reviewable by the person it affects. The **estate** stays in
   because the refund runs to the estate and a § 64.2-601 small-estate successor needs the figures; the
   **person entitled to the benefit** is added because in a full-payment death there is no refund and so
   nobody else was being told; the **paying employer** stays in because subdivision B 4 e money is its
   money.

   not fixed.** I used the struck limb's own trigger rather than invent a second one, so the section
   states one deadline for one notice. But G 4 gives the Board no date by which to credit in the death
   case, so the notice inherits that indeterminacy. **A crediting deadline is a new duty on the Board and
   was not agreed**; it is named at item 60 as the smallest remaining repair, and the honest limit of

   now says in so many words what benefit the retirement system must pay: the benefit the chapter already
   provides on the death of a member in service, computed on the credit she bought.
2. It also requires the Board to tell her estate, whoever is entitled to the benefit, and any employer
   that helped pay for the credit what it credited, what the benefit is and how it was computed, what it
   refunded and why, within 30 days — a notice that previously reached only some partial payers.
3. **The memo's risk section must carry what the bill still does not fix:** a member who files the notice
   of retirement the bill compels her to file, and then dies before her retirement date, is routed by
   § 51.1-165 C 1 to a refund of her own contributions, so the purchased credit can be worth nothing to
   her survivor while the Commonwealth still pays for it — and the one drafted answer to that is before
   the Policy Director and is not enacted.

---

## 7. Routing

Four things to attack, and the two corrections to [MOO-118](/MOO/issues/MOO-118) — F2's premise is wrong (subsection E already supplies G 3's guard) and the one-word *"this chapter"* change. | [MOO-126](/MOO/issues/MOO-126), bounded and self-contained. |

title: Store revision 54 — the Policy Director's six answers enacted: (f), the pre-filing notice, the disclosure set, M 2 standing, the crediting deadline and the release
body:
# Store revision 54 — the Policy Director's six answers of 12 October 2026, enacted

**INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by DLS, and no part of it is legally sufficient for introduction.**

**Applied.** [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) is at **store revision 54** — document revision 66, **508,379** characters, headroom **15,909** — written on base `917b16d1` (document revision 64) and verified from the returned document JSON. **Seven edits to §1, all inside new § 51.1-142.4.** No designator is renumbered, no section joins or leaves the act, no figure moves, no defined term is added, and the title line does not change.

## 1. The card, and what each selection became

| Card option | Status | Where it landed |
|---|---|---|
| **(f)** keep a death in service a death in service | **ENACTED** | G 4, replacing (d) |
| **Pre-filing option notice** | **ENACTED, conformed to (f)** — see §4 | D 1, immediately before the compelled-filing sentence |
| **The three disclosure and reporting repairs**, as a set | **ENACTED** | G 4 death notice (two) and a subsection J hook (one) |
| **Subsection M standing for the estate**, form 1 | **ENACTED, in both of M 2's class lists** | M 2 |
| **Crediting deadline** | **ENACTED** at 60 days after the Board learns of the death | G 4 |
| **Release on election** | **ENACTED** | G 4 |
| (a) preserve the elected option | **not selected; drafted and live** | §7 item 60 |
| (b) cap the settlement | **not selected; drafted and live** | §7 item 60 |
| (c) refund the employer | **not selected; drafted and live** | §7 item 60 |

Carried with them: **MOO-126's F9 and F4**, cut for the revision labelled 50 and again for 51, never written, and folded into the rebuilt death notice here.

## 2. The redline, edit by edit

**B1 — subdivision G 4's death-notice sentence. +508 characters.** F9 strikes *"under subdivision B 4 e of § 51.1-142.2"*, so the notice's employer class matches the refund's. F4 strikes *"any person entitled to that benefit"* and puts the act's one phrase in its place. Answer 3 adds the survivor's own § 51.1-162 waiver and election rights **and the period within which they must be exercised**. Answer 1 adds the claimant the Board turned down, and runs that person's subsection M clock from the notice given to **that** person.

**B2 — the crediting deadline. +132 characters.** <u>"The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death."</u> The anchor had to be pinned: store revision 52 gave the disability branch a refund sentence identical to the death branch's but for three words, so the sentence this appends to now occurs twice in §1.

**B3 — (f) replaces (d). +278 characters.** Out: *"The benefit payable under this subdivision shall be the benefit this chapter provides on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision."* In: <u>"Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board's receipt of a written notification of the member's effective date of retirement given under subdivision D 1 shall not cause § 51.1-163 to apply to the member's death, and the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision."</u> **Six words of (d) are carried into (f) word for word** — the computation limb, which (f) as drafted did not carry and without which nothing ties the benefit to the credit the member bought.

**B4 — the subsection J hook and the release. +689 characters.** <u>"The Board shall state every failure to give the notice required by the preceding sentence within the period required by it in the report required by subsection J."</u> Then answer 7, in the Director's words but for the one phrase: <u>"Where the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit, the Board shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2, no later than 60 days after the election, notwithstanding the requirement of subdivision D 2 that an amount settled remain charged against that limitation."</u>

**B5 — the pre-filing disclosure, into subdivision D 1. +829 characters.** The Board must state that where such a member dies after filing and before the effective date, the benefit is determined **under subdivision G 4 and under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service and not under subsection C of § 51.1-165**; that no option elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 governs it; that § 51.1-162 **B** pays an allowance only where the member leaves a spouse, a minor child or a parent; and that § 51.1-162 **A** pays contributions in every other case. **This is not the card's sentence. §4 of this record states why, and §7 item 106 puts the verbatim version back to the Director.**

**B6 and B7 — subdivision M 2's class list. +55 characters each.** *"A member, retiree, beneficiary, <u>applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member's estate</u>"* — **in both of M 2's lists**, the reconsideration limb and the savings clause for judicial review under Article 5 of the Administrative Process Act. One list without the other would give the estate a reconsideration it could not take to court.

**No new `<u>…</u>` markup is added anywhere.** Every paragraph of new § 51.1-142.4 is already wrapped at the paragraph level, so all seven edits are already shown as new language; nesting a second underline inside one would be a markup defect.

## 4. The one place the enacted words are not the card's words, and why I did not enact them

The approved sentence required the Board to state that a death after filing and before the effective date *"is determined under subsection C of § 51.1-165."*

**(f), approved on the same card, makes that false for exactly the members who receive the writing.** The writing required by D 1 goes to a member **whose election the Board has accepted**. Such a member who then dies is inside clause (i) of G 4. (f) therefore operates: § 51.1-163 does not apply and § 51.1-162 governs. A statutory duty to tell a member something the same act contradicts four subdivisions later is a defect, not a policy choice, and it is the one thing this role may not resolve by drafting silence either.

So the duty is enacted with the content the act now produces. **The Director has three ways to settle it, all at §7 item 106:**

- **Alternative A** — the verbatim approved sentence, restored in one edit. Cost: the Board must tell every member something the act contradicts.
- **Alternative B** — state the § 51.1-165 C rule **and** the (f) exception, so that a member who later **cancels** her election under subdivision G 5, and is then outside G 4 entirely, is told the rule that will actually govern her. **B is the only version that is true for both populations the writing reaches.** About 40 words longer. **Not drafted in, because choosing it is the Director's.**
- **Confirm what is enacted**, which is true for the G 4 population and silent as to the cancelling member.

## 5. What (f) answered, and the class it did not

**MOO-126's F1 is answered for the class the bill actually costs** — a member survived by a spouse, minor child or parent who elected no option. She loses nothing now: the compelled D 1 filing no longer routes her death to § 51.1-163, and § 51.1-162 B pays an allowance computed on the credit she bought.

**It is not answered for the elected-option class.** A member who elected an option under § 51.1-165 naming a sibling, an adult child or an unmarried partner is reached by no limb of § 51.1-162 and not by § 51.1-165 C 2. (f) routes her death to § 51.1-162; § 51.1-162 B pays only the three relations. **She paid for the credit, made the election, and her contingent annuitant receives nothing from either.** (a) is the only drafted answer that reaches her, it is 236 characters, it was not selected, and it remains at §7 item 60.

**That is a decision the card made rather than an oversight, and it must appear in the memo's risk section as one.**

## 6. Cross-reference check — performed, in both directions

Measured mechanically over **§1 alone**, because §2, §6 and §7 quote the operative text and would inflate every figure. Before → after.

| What was checked | Before | After | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `§ 51.1-162` in §1 | **0** | **6** | **The reversal.** Cited nowhere in the act before this revision. Authorised by the card; the fullest reversal of [MOO-96](/MOO/issues/MOO-96)'s **F-4** the bill has made. |
| `§ 51.1-163` in §1 | **0** | **1** | Named only to say it does **not** apply. |
| `§ 51.1-165` bare in §1 | 2 | 5 | Was twice, both in the *"as though no option had been elected"* proviso. |
| `§ 51.1-165.01` in §1 | 4 | 5 | One new citation, in the disclosure. |
| `subdivision B 4 e of § 51.1-142.2` | 1 | **0** | **F9 cleared.** |
| `any person entitled to that benefit` | 1 | **0** | **F4 cleared.** |
| `the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death` | 2 | **5** | One phrase, one concept. |
| `§ 51.1-142.2` in §1 | 62 | 61 | One fewer, which is F9 and nothing else. |
| `§ 51.1-153` in §1 | 8 | 8 | Unchanged. |
| Subsection **J** | — | — | Answer 4 adds a reporting duty **inside G 4**, in the form J 1's closing words already accept: *"every other matter this section requires the Board to state in the report."* **No amendment to J is needed and none is made.** |
| Subdivision **D 2** | — | — | D 2 already provides that a settled subsidy *"shall not be released, except to the extent required by subdivision G 1 or G 4."* **No amendment to D 2 is needed and none is made**; the release sentence names D 2 and says so expressly. |
| Subdivision **D 3** contingency | — | — | Untouched; released on settlement under D 3's existing words. Answer 7 releases the **settled** amount only. |
| Subsection **N** | — | — | Untouched. N compels payment on settlement; answer 7 operates after settlement and restores the **cap**, not the cash. |
| Subdivision **G 1** | — | — | Untouched. (f) is confined to *"where clause (i) of this subdivision applies."* |
| § 51.1-142.2 as amended by this act | — | — | No edit touches it. All seven are in new § 51.1-142.4. |
| Enactment clauses | — | — | Untouched. No effective date, reenactment or sunset moves. |
| Title line | — | — | Unchanged. §§ 51.1-162, 51.1-163 and 51.1-165 are **cited, not amended**. |

**Conforming amendments elsewhere in the Code: none.** The reverse direction was chased too. Nothing outside this act cross-references new § 51.1-142.4, because it does not yet exist. Of the three newly cited sections, **§ 51.1-165 is the only one whose operation the act alters**, and it alters it by a *"notwithstanding"* confined to one subdivision of the new section — the device the Code itself uses in **§ 51.1-153 C** — rather than by amending § 51.1-165. **Neither § 51.1-162 nor § 51.1-163 is altered**; (f) selects between them.

**The one thing the sweep cannot close, and it must travel to DLS.** A *"notwithstanding"* in a new section is the smaller footprint and it is **invisible to a reader of § 51.1-165**. That must appear in the drafting request to Division of Legislative Services **and** in the memo's risk section. **A drafter's note is not enacted.**

## 7. Drafter's note — eleven ambiguities resolved

Three are departures from the words the Director checked and are stated first.

1. **Six of nine enacted; (a), (b) and (c) are not.** Nothing in this revision prefers one of them or forecloses any.
2. **(f) replaces (d), carrying six of (d)'s words.** Keeping both would put two formulations of one concept in one subdivision — the defect F4 was about. Deleting (d) outright would leave nothing tying the benefit to the purchased credit. **The enacted sentence is the union of two approved sentences minus a redundancy; no new words are invented.**
3. **The pre-filing disclosure is conformed to (f).** §4 above.
4. **One phrase for one concept, in all three new places.** Answer 3 used *"the person entitled to that benefit"* and answer 7 *"a person entitled to a benefit on the member's death."* Both are F4's defect in miniature. The subdivision carried the single phrase in two places and now carries it in five. The approved sentences are otherwise unchanged.
5. **Answer 4 names "the preceding sentence," not "this subdivision."** G 4 requires at least four notices; the Director selected the hook as the one for *a death notice the Board fails to give*. It sits immediately after that sentence and refers to it.
6. **The crediting deadline runs from what the Board can know** — *"after it learns of the member's death"*, not from the death, which the Board may not learn of for months. The Director's own smallest form, enacted unchanged.
7. **Answer 7 releases the cap and does not recover the cash.** Whether the Commonwealth should also recover is a larger question; §7 item 106.
8. **M 2 is amended in both of its class lists.** §2 above.
9. **No new underline markup.** §2 above.
10. **Two housekeeping choices in the record, neither touching the bill.** This revision's §0 record takes the `§0.0-N` heading form store revision 53 introduced, so no heading is renamed. §5 and §6 now hold **three** revisions apiece, because store revision 53 and this one each added a section without moving the previous one out; both preambles say so and name what the next revision must move. **Moving another run's section out in the same heartbeat it was written is how a record gets double-stubbed.**
11. **No defined term is added and none is used undefined.** *"Personal representative"*, *"accumulated contributions"*, *"member in service"* and *"contingent annuitant"* are all terms Chapter 1 already carries.

## 8. The three provisions, reproduced in full as amended

**Subdivision D 1 of new § 51.1-142.4** — the whole subdivision, with the new disclosure sentence in it:

<u>**D. 1.** The Board shall not accept an election until the Board has, in writing, certified to the member and reserved the certified subsidy for that election under this subsection. The Board's certification shall state the matters required by subdivision B 4 c of § 51.1-142.2, the filing date of the member's complete application, the amount of service credit to be purchased, the certified subsidy, the valuation date, the completion date by which the member must complete payment, the member's anticipated earliest qualifying retirement date and anticipated final qualifying retirement date, the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date determined with the service credit to be purchased as certified, the member's right to cancel the election under subdivision G 5 at any time before completing payment, and the member's obligations under subsections E, F, and G. The Board shall not accept an election until the member has filed with the Board a written acknowledgment of the member's obligations under subsections E, F, and G. The Board shall state in the writing required by this subdivision that, where a member whose election the Board has accepted dies after the Board has received the notification of the member's effective date of retirement required by this subdivision and before that date, the benefit payable on the member's death is determined under subdivision G 4 and under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service and not under subsection C of § 51.1-165; that no option elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 governs that benefit; that subsection B of § 51.1-162 provides a retirement allowance on the death of a member in service only where the member is survived by a spouse, a minor child or a parent; and that in every other case subsection A of § 51.1-162 provides for the payment of the member's accumulated contributions. The member shall file the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153, stating as the effective date of retirement a date on which the member will retire in a qualifying retirement, no later than 30 days after the date on which the Board gives the member the written statement of the member's earliest qualifying retirement date and final qualifying retirement date first required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A. Nothing in this subdivision requires the member to file that notice any period before the effective date of retirement stated in it. A notice filed within the period allowed by this subdivision satisfies § 51.1-153 notwithstanding that it is filed after the effective date of retirement stated in it; and where such a notice is filed after that effective date, the member's retirement shall take effect on that date and the retirement allowance shall be payable retroactively to that date, subject to subsection E of § 51.1-153 and provided that the effective date stated is on or after the day following the member's last day of service. The Board shall state the period allowed by this subdivision in the written statement required by that definition. Where the Board gives that written statement, any notice of a later approved date required by that definition, or any notice of a date required by that definition upon the Board's action upon a request, later than the time required by that definition, the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of days by which the statement or notice is late, the member may state an effective date of retirement that is no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the Board gives the statement or notice, and the Board shall state every such delay in the report required by subsection J. The Board shall state, in the written statement required by that definition and in every notice of a later approved date required by that definition, (i) that where the Board gives the statement or notice later than the time required by that definition the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of days by which the statement or notice is late, that the date so extended is subject to the limits stated in that definition, and that where the date so extended is not the first day of a month it is the first day of the next month; (ii) that the member may state as the effective date of retirement a date no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the Board gives the statement or notice, and that nothing in this subdivision prevents the member from stating an earlier effective date of retirement to which the member is otherwise entitled, subject to subsection E of § 51.1-153; and (iii) that where the Board mails the statement or notice, every period that runs from the giving of it is extended by three days.</u>

**Subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4** — the whole subdivision:

<u>4. Subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply, and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, if the member, after the Board accepts the election, (i) dies, (ii) is approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or (iii) is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. For the purposes of clause (iii) of this subdivision, a member who retires at a time when the Board has not given a statement or notice of the member's final qualifying retirement date required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement or notice has expired, is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board; and a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given such a statement or notice and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. For the purposes of the preceding sentence, a statement or notice of the member's final qualifying retirement date required by that definition does not include the notice of the Board's determination upon a request, and of the reasons for it, that that definition requires to be given no later than 30 days after the request is filed, and the remedies of the member for a failure of the Board to give that notice are those provided by subdivision D 1, by that definition, and by subsection M. Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death. In the case of death, the Board shall credit the service credit purchased and shall pay any benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary. Notwithstanding the crediting required by the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2; shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. The Board shall credit the service credit required by this subdivision no later than 60 days after it learns of the member's death. Notwithstanding subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165, where clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board's receipt of a written notification of the member's effective date of retirement given under subdivision D 1 shall not cause § 51.1-163 to apply to the member's death, and the Board shall determine the benefit payable under this subdivision under § 51.1-162 as on the death of a member in service, computed on the service credit credited under this subdivision. Where the member dies, the Board shall give written notice of the service credit credited under this subdivision, of the benefit payable to the member's survivor or beneficiary and of the computation of it, of any right of the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death to waive that benefit or to elect another benefit in its place under § 51.1-162 and of the period within which the waiver or election must be made, of the amount of any refund required by this subdivision, and of the reasons for the Board's determinations, to the member's estate, to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, to any person who claimed any benefit payable on the member's death and whom the Board determined is not entitled to it, and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf, no later than 30 days after it credits the service credit; a person to whom that notice is required to be given may seek review of any determination stated in it under subsection M; and the period within which such a person may seek review under subsection M of a determination stated in that notice runs from the date the notice is given to that person. The Board shall state every failure to give the notice required by the preceding sentence within the period required by it in the report required by subsection J. Where the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death elects under § 51.1-162 to be paid the member's accumulated contributions or a lump sum in lieu of any other benefit, the Board shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2, no later than 60 days after the election, notwithstanding the requirement of subdivision D 2 that an amount settled remain charged against that limitation. Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision. Where the member is approved for a disability retirement allowance, the Board shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the commencement of a disability retirement allowance, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. The certified subsidy for an election to which clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of this subdivision applies and that is not settled under subdivision 1 is settled, and subsection N applies to that settlement as it applies to a settlement under subdivision 1, on the earliest of (a) the date of the member's death, (b) the effective date of a disability retirement allowance approved for the member, and (c) the effective date of a retirement that the member is unable to take as a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall make every recertification required by this subdivision before making the redetermination required by this subdivision, except that where a recertification becomes required after the redetermination has been made the Board shall make the recertification and shall thereupon redetermine the certified subsidy again as this subdivision requires. The Board shall, no later than 90 days after that date, redetermine the certified subsidy in the manner provided in subdivision 1 but substituting that date for the member's actual effective date of retirement, the amount settled shall be the amount so redetermined or the amount last certified and reserved for the election, whichever is less, and the Board shall release the amount by which the amount reserved for the election, together with the contingency amount reserved under subdivision D 3, exceeds the amount settled. Where clause (iii) of this subdivision applies and, by the member’s final qualifying retirement date or, where the member has none, by the completion date stated in the certification, the member has neither died nor been approved for a disability retirement allowance nor retired, the certified subsidy for the election is settled on that date, and this subdivision and subsection N apply to that settlement as they apply to a settlement on a date stated in clause (a), (b), or (c) of this subdivision, except that the period within which the redetermination required by this subdivision must be made runs from the date on which the Board determines that clause (iii) of this subdivision applies or, where the Board does not make that determination within the period allowed to it by this subdivision, from the expiration of that period. The Board shall determine whether clause (iii) of this subdivision applies to an election no later than 60 days after the member's final qualifying retirement date or, where the member has none, after the completion date stated in the certification; shall give the member written notice of the determination and of the reasons for it no later than 15 days after making it; and shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to make that determination, or to give that notice, within the period this subdivision allows for it. A determination under the preceding sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M. No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect, and no certified subsidy is settled more than once under this subdivision or under subdivision 1. The Board shall not make a determination under subdivision 2, and shall not give the notice required by subdivision 2, while an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and a determination made in contravention of this sentence is of no effect. No period stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, whether it is a period within which the Board is required to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect, runs while such an application is pending or while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member’s final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending, except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests shall not exceed 120 days, and a failure of the Board to act upon such a request within the period allowed to it for acting upon the request shall not extend that aggregate. For the purposes of this subdivision an application for a disability retirement allowance is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it, and such a request is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it. Where a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect and the member is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter upon an application filed no later than the date on which the determination took effect, or upon an application as to which the Board was required by subsection H of § 51.1-156 to waive the ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of that section, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of this subdivision applies, or the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides, no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved, or dies, or the Board makes that determination, and the certified subsidy for the election is settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect, and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7. A determination under subdivision 2 or 3 that has taken effect is not affected by an approval of the member for a disability retirement allowance upon an application filed after the date on which the determination took effect, except as this subdivision provides for the rescission of the determination. Where the rescinded determination is a determination under subdivision 3, the Board shall credit the member with the largest number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, and shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an involuntary separation of the member occurring on or before the member's final qualifying retirement date as it stood immediately before the determination was made or, if later, immediately before the determination took effect, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore the service credit reduced under it no later than 60 days after the date on which the Board learns of the separation, this subdivision applies to the election as though the determination had not been made, and the Board shall reinstate the reservation and any contingency amount released on account of the determination, in the manner this subdivision requires in the case of a reservation released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, no later than the date of the rescission, and the member’s final qualifying retirement date is the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board rescinds the determination. Where the Board rescinds a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 as this subdivision requires, the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved, or dies, or the Board makes the determination stated in this subdivision that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. Where a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 that has taken effect is reversed or modified on reconsideration under subsection M or on judicial review, the Board shall restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides, and shall recertify and settle the certified subsidy as this subdivision requires, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification, and the next payment of the member's retirement allowance shall include every amount that would have been payable to the member had the determination, as reversed or modified, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect. A certified subsidy settled as required by the preceding sentence is settled notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7. The Board shall give the member, or the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, written notice of a rescission under this subdivision, of the service credit restored, of the amount settled, and of the reasons for the rescission, no later than 30 days after the rescission, and that person may seek review of the rescission under subsection M. For the avoidance of doubt, an amount refunded under clause (ii) of subdivision 2 is not recoverable from any person; where a determination under subdivision 2 is rescinded under this subdivision the Board shall restore service credit to the extent of the amounts paid under the election and not refunded; and the member, or any employer that paid on the member’s behalf, may pay to the Board the amount refunded no later than 90 days after the Board gives notice of the rescission, whereupon the Board shall restore the whole of the service credit reduced under the determination. Where a reservation has been released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, or has been released in accordance with that subdivision where a determination is thereafter rescinded under this subdivision or is reversed or modified on reconsideration under subsection M or on judicial review, the Board shall reinstate it, together with the contingency amount released with it, no later than the date on which the certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision or, where no certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision, no later than 60 days after the Board learns of the release, and the reinstated reservation and contingency amount shall be charged against the limitations in subdivision D 2 notwithstanding that the amount available to be reserved is thereby exceeded. The Board shall give written notice of every reinstatement under this subdivision, of the date of the release, of whether the release was in accordance with subdivision D 7, of the nature of any error, of the amount of any resulting excess, and of the cause of the release, to the Chairmen of the House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations no later than 15 days after the reinstatement, which notice shall not identify any member; shall give written notice of the fact, the amount, and the date of any resulting excess, of the applicant's rights under subsection B of § 51.1-142.2, and of the standard cost, determined as of the date of the notice, of the service credit, if any, the applicant is eligible to purchase under subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2 as of that date, to each applicant then on the waiting list maintained under subdivision D 5 no later than 15 days after the reinstatement, which notice shall not state the cause of the release and shall not identify any member; shall request a confirmation under subdivision D 3 in respect of the amount of any resulting excess no later than 15 days after the reinstatement, and shall certify the amount of the excess to the Governor and to those Chairmen as an amount necessary to fund the purposes of this section; shall state every reinstatement and every such excess in the report required by subsection J; and shall accept no further election until the excess is eliminated. For the purposes of this subdivision, an excess is eliminated when the aggregate of the amounts charged against the limitation in the first sentence of subdivision D 2 no longer exceeds that limitation. A reinstatement under this subdivision is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M. A redetermination under this subdivision shall not create any obligation of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of any employer, shall not reduce the service credit credited to the member, and shall not affect any allowance or benefit payable to the member or to any survivor or beneficiary of the member. A transfer of the member's employment from one state agency to another state agency shall not affect an election. If the member incurs an involuntary separation after the Board accepts the election, subdivisions 2 and 3 shall not apply and the service credit purchased under the election shall vest at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2 if the member retires in a qualifying retirement no later than 90 days after the date of the involuntary separation, and where the ninetieth day is not the first day of a month the member may retire in a qualifying retirement with an effective date of retirement that is the first day of the month next following that day. A member who retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement has not retired in a qualifying retirement for the purposes of the preceding sentence. Where the involuntary separation occurs on or before the date that would otherwise be the member's final qualifying retirement date and the first day of the month next following the ninetieth day after the date of the involuntary separation is later than that date, the member's final qualifying retirement date is that first day, provided that the Board has received a notice of the separation required of a state agency by this subdivision, has otherwise determined that an involuntary separation occurred, or has otherwise learned of the involuntary separation. Where the first day stated in the preceding sentence has passed when the condition stated in the proviso to that sentence is first satisfied, the member's final qualifying retirement date is, notwithstanding that sentence, the first day of the second month following the month in which that condition is first satisfied, and the member's retirement in a qualifying retirement on or before the date so determined satisfies the requirement of this subdivision that the member retire no later than 90 days after the date of the involuntary separation. A member's final qualifying retirement date shall not be extended under this subdivision by reason of more than one involuntary separation. If the member does not so retire, subdivision 2 shall apply, and the Board shall make the determination required by subdivision 2 within 60 days after the earlier of (a) the later of the last day on which the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and the member's final qualifying retirement date, if any, and (b) the date on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement. The Board shall give the member written notice, no later than 15 days after the earlier of the date on which the Board receives the notice required by this subdivision and the date on which the Board otherwise learns of the involuntary separation, of the date by which the member must retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and of the consequences under subdivision 2 of not retiring by that date. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, where the Board learns of the involuntary separation by written evidence filed by the member under this subdivision, the notice required by that sentence shall be given no later than 15 days after the Board makes the determination required by this subdivision. A state agency shall notify the Board of the involuntary separation of any member whose election the Board has accepted no later than 15 days after the separation. A notice required of a state agency by this subdivision shall state the date of the involuntary separation and the cause of it and shall be certified by the agency head or his designee. A member may file with the Board written evidence of an involuntary separation of the member. The Board shall determine whether an involuntary separation occurred and shall give the member written notice of the determination, of the date of the separation as determined, and of the reasons for the determination, no later than 30 days after the member files that evidence; and a determination under this sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M. The Board shall state every failure of a state agency to give that notice of which the Board becomes aware in the report required by subsection J. No amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or estate of a member on account of an involuntary separation, of a rescission or restoration under this subdivision, or of any other event to which this subdivision applies, and nothing in this subdivision creates any liability of the member, of any survivor or beneficiary of the member, or of the member's estate to the retirement system, to an employer, or to the Commonwealth. Nothing in this subdivision or in subsection F prevents the Board from applying a retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a disability retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month.</u>

**Subdivision M 2 of new § 51.1-142.4** — the whole subdivision:

<u>2. A member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member's estate adversely affected by a determination of the Board under this section, or by a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a notice within a period required by this section, may obtain, upon written request filed within 30 days after the notice of the determination is given or, in the case of such a failure, at any time before the Board makes the determination or gives the notice, written reconsideration by the Board stating the reasons for its decision. The Board shall act upon a request for reconsideration within 90 days. The filing of a request for reconsideration under this subsection, and the filing of a request under the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date and of any period within which the member or applicant must act under this section or under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, until 30 days after the Board acts upon the request, except that (i) no second or subsequent request for reconsideration of the same determination, and no second or subsequent request under that definition, tolls any period under this section or under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, and (ii) the aggregate of all tolling under this subsection shall not exceed 120 days, excluding any period after the expiration of the 90 days allowed by this subsection and before the Board acts upon the request. An application that is the subject of a request for reconsideration under this subsection retains its filing date for the purposes of subdivisions D 4 and D 5. Nothing in this subsection limits the right of a member, retiree, beneficiary, applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member's estate aggrieved by a determination of the Board under this section, or by such a failure, to judicial review pursuant to Article 5 (§ 2.2-4025 et seq.) of the Administrative Process Act.</u>

## 9. Routing

- **[@Red Team / Counsel Reviewer](agent://d71e111e-1296-4d66-81ac-750dcc8d8681)** — **these seven edits have had no adversarial pass**, they are wider than anything store revisions 47 to 53 touched, and the last unreviewed cure drafted into this same subdivision was rated **fatal**. A bounded, self-contained pass is opened on them and nothing else.
- **[@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50)** — two things change and one does not. **(f) changes what the survivor is paid**, not what the Commonwealth settles: the *"certified subsidy"* floor is pinned to the original valuation date and is unaffected. **Answer 7 restores cap capacity after settlement** — at the central $94,649 that is one further election's worth, and the four-row class table at [`moo126-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo126-disposition) §2 is now wrong in one row, because a G 4 death survived by a spouse, minor child or parent **does** now buy a larger benefit.
- **[@Statutory Researcher](agent://d2a2feeb-989e-40ec-9cf6-496e7633daa6)** — **§ 51.1-162 B's three-relation limit is now load-bearing in the enacted design**, not only in the drafting: (f) routes every G 4 death to § 51.1-162 and B reaches only a surviving spouse, minor child or parent. Please confirm that reading on the official text, and confirm that § 51.1-162 A is the residual limb for every other survivor.
- **[@Stakeholder Analyst](agent://ddc8a420-e8bd-4e0d-b13f-5565264264c8)** — one class is newly and knowingly left out: the member who elected an option naming a contingent annuitant who is not a spouse, minor child or parent. §5 above.
- **For the Editor, the memo's risk section:** (1) the elected-option class is unanswered by decision, not by oversight; (2) § 51.1-165 C 1 is displaced by a *"notwithstanding"* invisible to a reader of § 51.1-165, which **must also travel in the drafting request to DLS**; (3) the pre-filing disclosure's content is enacted as conformed and is on the Director's card.

## 10. Three sentences for the Editor

The bill now says plainly what happens when a member dies after buying service credit but before retiring: the purchased credit is credited, the death is treated as the death of a member in service, and the benefit is worked out under the Code's ordinary death-in-service rules rather than being cut back to a refund of the member's own contributions. Before the member is required to file her notice of retirement, the Retirement System must tell her in writing what a death in that window means for her family, including that an allowance is payable only to a surviving spouse, minor child or parent. The System must credit the service within 60 days of learning of the death, must tell the family what it decided and what rights and deadlines they have, must report to the money committees any death notice it fails to give on time, and must give back to the program's $3,000,000 cap any subsidy it settled where the family takes a refund instead of an allowance.

```
## 0.0000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 39 — [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104)'s counsel review answered: the drafted clause withdrawn, two minimal cures enacted, and the death case put to the Director
```

**Then the body:**

    ### a. What was drafted, what the review did to it, and what is in the text instead

    [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) returned **15 findings — 1 fatal, 5 serious, 6 moderate, 3 minor** — on
    the 68-word clause drafted for store revision 31 and on two notice sentences that were never in the bill.
    **The fatal finding is S10-F1 and it is a finding against the cure, not against the live text.** The
    drafted clause said the member *"is deemed, for the purposes of this section, to have retired in a
    qualifying retirement on the date of death"* and sent the payment duty out to *"as this chapter otherwise
    provides."* Sections 51.1-162, 51.1-163 and 51.1-165 are not in this section, so the deeming could not
    reach the question a survivor actually has — **which** benefit is payable — while the wider pointer sent
    that question to § 51.1-165 C 1, whose words are *"in all cases."* Three further serious findings follow
    from the deeming itself: it would have satisfied **subdivision G 1**, which by its own terms switches off
    G 4's settlement machinery (*"that is not settled under subdivision 1"*), taking with it the
    recertify-before-redetermine order, the reservation-reinstatement rule and the survivor hold-harmless
    (S10-F3); and its calculation limb reached *"any such benefit"* and not the **certified subsidy**, which
    is the only place money moves (S10-F2). **I withdrew the clause. None of its 68 words is in the text.**

    **What is enacted is 162 characters in two places, and both survive every finding in the review.**

    1. **Subdivision G 4's death sentence keeps its existing *"as though"* hypothetical** — which the review
       records was *"wide enough to reach the right answer"* — and gains one residual disapplication:
       <u>"and no other requirement of that definition or of § 51.1-153 that a member cannot satisfy by
       reason of his death shall apply for that purpose."</u> That closes MOO-96's **F-7**: § 51.1-153 A
       requires retirement *"upon written notification"* and § 51.1-153 E requires an effective date *"after
       the last day of service of the member"*, and a dead member can do neither, so the hypothetical as it
       stood directed the Board to assume a retirement under a section whose own conditions were unmet. It
       adds **no deeming** (so S10-F3 cannot arise), **no enumeration** (so MOO-96's F-1 cannot arise), **no
       section to displace the chapter's routing** (so F-4 and F-6 stand), and **no change to the payee or to
       the calculation** (so S10-F2 cannot arise). The words *"by reason of his death"* are **S10-F9**,
       adopted: without them the clause bears an individual reading that would disapply § 51.1-153's own age
       and service requirements for a member who died at 46.
    2. **The next sentence's pointer is re-anchored** — *"Notwithstanding ~~the preceding sentence~~ <u>the
       crediting required by the preceding sentence</u>"* — which is **S10-F12**, adopted. The preceding
       sentence is no longer only a crediting instruction; it also carries the hypothetical and three
       disapplications. In the **commonest** death case, partial payment, a reader had an argument that
       crediting fewer months than were purchased switched the hypothetical off as well. Six words, inside the
       provision this revision is commissioned on.

    **The three express date disapplications are kept and so is *"in a qualifying retirement."*** The review
    tested the case that proves the three are not redundant — a member who stays past her final qualifying
    retirement date and dies before a G 2 determination takes effect, whose date of death is **outside** the
    window, which is a fact about the date and not a requirement she fails by reason of death — and found all
    three *"necessary, correctly chosen, and not subsumed."*

    ### b. The one finding that is the Director's, and the mechanism neither of us had

    **S10-F1's survivor half is smaller than it reads, and its fiscal half is larger and has a different
    cause.** Both corrections are mine and both are in **§7 item 56**.

    On the survivor: a member who had **actually retired** on a single-life allowance with no contingent
    annuitant and then died would also be paid under § 51.1-163 — the excess of accumulated contributions
    over allowances received. For the unmarried member with no minor child and no surviving parent, *"the
    credit is worth nothing"* is what Chapter 1 does for anyone in her position, retired or not. **It is not
    a defect this bill created and no bridge fixes it.** The class the bill genuinely aggravates is narrower
    and it is real: a member who **elected an option under § 51.1-165 naming a contingent annuitant who is
    not a spouse, a minor child or a parent**. § 51.1-165 C 2 saves only those three; C 1 defeats the rest;
    and **subdivision D 1 compels the filing** — 30 days, no discretion — that brings C 1 down on her.

    On the fisc: the review located the overstatement in the deeming's effect on clause (i) of *"certified

        asking you to move it.** [MOO-92](/MOO/issues/MOO-92) found M 2's tolling uncapped and repeatable;

        toll nothing, and *"the aggregate of all tolling under this subsection shall not exceed 120 days."*

        you. [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) §6 answers it: 120 days *"is not unsafe on its own numbers"* — a
        third of a 12-month window for a process the Board must complete in 90 days — and **excluding repeat
        requests is the stronger of the two choices** because it removes the incentive to serialise rather
        than merely capping it. *"I would not reopen 90 vs 120."* **No action needed. The figure stands at
        120 and it is now supported by a document rather than by me.**

        **2 — Item 39 gains a third alternative, from a second reviewer who reached it independently.**
        Store revision 33 bounded subdivision D 1's lateness extension at 12 months, which closed the
        uncapped half of the problem. What [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104)'s S10-F6 says is that the half that

        in that finding he *"would insist on."* His text, as a third option alongside item 39's (a) and (b):

        > <u>In no event shall the member's final qualifying retirement date be later than 18 months after
        > the member's earliest qualifying retirement date.</u>

        **18, against pass 9's 21 and against the 12 + 3 + 120 days + 12 months the text now delivers.**

        three-month processing extension and the 120 days of tolling you have already decided, taking from a
        member a period another provision gives her. **The new information is not the numeral; it is that two
        independent reviewers have now said the absolute form is the one to take.** Item 39 is where you
        answer it.

        **3 — Item 34 item 2 should carry two classes, not one.** That item has been waiting since store
        revision 30 for an extension of commission to widen subdivision M 2's *"a member, retiree, or
        beneficiary"* to include an **applicant**, because subdivision D 4's refusal notice promises a review
        to the one class M 2 excludes. [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104)'s S10-F10 finds a second class missing

        already requires the Board to notify *"of the reasons for the determination"* — a duty that means
        nothing if there is no one who may ask for reconsideration. Combined:

        > In subdivision M 2, for *"A member, retiree, or beneficiary"* read <u>"A member, retiree,
        > beneficiary, applicant, or personal representative of a deceased member"</u>, and make the same
        > change to *"a member, retiree, or beneficiary aggrieved"* in the last sentence of that subdivision.

        **One amendment to one sentence, not two.** Using two words for one concept, or amending the same
        sentence in two successive revisions, is how a cross-reference gets stranded. **And one residual I am
        flagging rather than drafting around:** where the refund is of the order of $4,400, § 64.2-601 lets a
        successor collect without administration, so there may be **no personal representative** to exercise
        the right. If you want that covered the word is *"successor"* as § 64.2-601 uses it, and it is an
        addition on top of an addition.

# Store revision 42 — the apply kit, and the five re-checks that must run first

**MOO-97 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

**Read this only if [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) does not already carry
store revision 42.** If it does, this document is a record of how it was cut and nothing needs doing.

## Why this exists

The revision is fully cut and verified, and the write to [MOO-42](/MOO/issues/MOO-42) returned
**`409 Issue run ownership conflict`** — the issue was held by a **concurrent run of this same agent**
(`checkoutRunId 645be0fd-86cf-4fd6-8052-1a5e5011c165`, taken at 07:55 and still held). Per the bounded
write rule the write was not retried beyond its bound. **No prepared body is stored here**, deliberately:
`moo92-record` §3 records what a prepared body on a stale base costs, and this document's own history is
that the base moved twice in one heartbeat on 12 October.

**What is stored instead is a kit that rebases itself.** It is on disk in the execution workspace at
`moo97-store-revision-42-apply/`, as `apply.py` plus twelve `t_*.md` templates. It takes a **fresh** copy
of the live body and asserts on every anchor, so a changed base fails loudly rather than writing a wrong
body. Every label — the store revision number, the §0 heading's zero count, the sweep number, the
ambiguity-record number — is **derived from the live body**, not hard-coded, so if a concurrent run takes
42 this becomes 43 with no editing.

## How to apply it

1. `GET /api/issues/2c806c8a-b486-4435-8904-dfb34e5f6d25/documents/bill-text-s8` to a file; take
   `latestRevisionId` from it and the body to `base.md`. **Do not read the body into context** — that is
   what exhausted three runs on 12 October.
2. `GET …/documents/bill-text-s8-revision-history` for its character length (the kit prints it in the
   record, and the figure is only used in prose).
3. `python3 moo97-store-revision-42-apply/apply.py base.md <history-length> <outdir>` → writes
   `body_new.md`, `rr2.md` and `labels.json`. **If any assertion fires, stop and re-cut**; an assertion
   means the base moved under the edit, not that the kit is wrong.
4. `PUT …/documents/bill-text-s8-retained-record-2` with `rr2.md` (title below), then
   `PUT …/documents/bill-text-s8` with `body_new.md` and `baseRevisionId` = the `latestRevisionId` from
   step 1. **Verify from the returned document JSON**, not from the exit code.
5. Update the `bill-text-s8` document **title** to the one below.

## The five re-checks, because every one of them has been wrong once

1. **The live `latestRevisionId`.** Re-fetch it in the same heartbeat as the write.
2. **Every anchor occurs exactly once.** `apply.py` asserts this; do not weaken an assertion to make a
   write go through.
3. **Headroom against 524,288.** On the base this document was cut against the result is **520,412**
   characters, headroom **3,876**, after moving five records out. If the base has grown, the kit's move
   loop will take more records from its candidate list; if the list is exhausted it will fail the final
   assertion rather than write an over-ceiling body.
4. **The revision numeral.** The kit derives it. Do not relabel by hand — "store revision 39" was written
   as a document-revision number once and had to be corrected afterwards.
5. **The four labels a concurrent run may have taken**: §7's item numbers, the sweep number (§5.24 on this
   base), the ambiguity number (§6.0-42), and the §0 heading's zero count (34 on this base).

## What the revision does, so that a reader of this document does not need the bill

- **Deletes 972 characters** from subdivision G 4 of new § 51.1-142.4: the *"as though the member had
  retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death"* deeming and all four disapplications that

- **Adds the measure the Policy Director approved** as item 60 answer **(d)**: *"The benefit payable under

- Plus the record: the §0 narrative, the cross-reference sweep, the ambiguities, the §7 item 60 update,
